# MCP tools

The pod's MCP server lists 98 tools. A new agent key lists the `entry` tools; the others arrive by group when an agent calls `synap_load_skill` with `tools:<group>` (or `tools:builder` for every group). A group narrows what is listed; it is not a permission. A call still runs under the key's scopes and the pod's governance.

## synap_ask

**Ask the pod** · Group: `entry` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

THE recall door. Ask the user's Synap pod anything in natural language — it routes across all knowledge substrates (entities/notes/tasks, how-to runbooks, remembered facts/preferences, and the links/files the user kept in their Library — found by what was read from them) and returns ONE provenance-tagged answer saying which substrate answered. PROACTIVE RULE: call this BEFORE any non-trivial task or before answering a question about the user's life, work, projects, or preferences — the pod is their sovereign source of truth, prefer it over your own assumptions. Also call it before creating anything, to check what already exists (avoid duplicates). This single tool replaces the old search/search_entities/recall_facts/get_knowledge tools.

| Parameter     | Type    | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `query`       | string  | yes      | Your question, in natural language                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `detail`      | enum    | no       | How much answer you want. full (default) = the provenance-rich answer. brief = a few sentences, no capture suggestions — use it for lookups (who/what/where). sources = no synthesis: the ranked { substrate, id, title } matches only, answer null; read one with synap_get_entity. One of: `sources`, `brief`, `full`. |
| `workspaceId` | string  | no       | Optional: scope to one workspace. Omit for pod-wide recall across everything the user has.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `projectId`   | string  | no       | Optional: scope recall to a project (its projects table id). Narrows results to entities linked to that project. Orthogonal to workspaceId — compose both lenses.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `limit`       | number  | no       | Max results per substrate (default: 10)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `compare`     | boolean | no       | A/B DIAGNOSTIC: run BOTH the baseline and Horizon rankers on the same candidate pool and return { baseline, horizon, diff:{ overlapAtN, moved } } instead of a synthesized answer. Read-only — does NOT change normal recall. For evaluating ranking changes.                                                            |

## synap_get_entities

**List entities** · Group: `read` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

List entities for a user filtered by profileSlug. Use to browse all entities of a type (all tasks, all projects). For content/semantic recall use synap_ask. Pages: `limit` (default 50) + `offset`; a reply with `nextOffset` has more — pass it back as `offset`. Returns lean rows by default; use synap_get_entity or detail:'full' for full values.

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `detail`      | enum   | no       | lean (default) = null columns and systemData omitted, string values over 120 chars truncated with '…[truncated: N chars total]' (every property key kept). full = unprojected rows. One of: `lean`, `full`. |
| `profileSlug` | string | no       | Profile slug filter (e.g. note, task, bookmark). Prefer this over `type`.                                                                                                                                   |
| `type`        | string | no       | Deprecated alias for profileSlug.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `workspaceId` | string | no       | Workspace ID (optional)                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `projectId`   | string | no       | Optional: narrow to a project (its entity id) — only entities belonging to it. Orthogonal to workspaceId; usually pre-set by the connection URL.                                                            |
| `facetSlug`   | string | no       | Kind + Facets filter — only return entities carrying a live facet of this role-profile slug (e.g. 'client', 'investor'). Use synap_list_profiles to find role slugs (profileKind='role').                   |
| `limit`       | number | no       | Page size, 1–999.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `offset`      | number | no       | Rows to skip — pass the previous reply's `nextOffset` to read the next page. No `nextOffset` in a reply means it was the last page.                                                                         |

## synap_get_document

**Get document** · Group: `read` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Get a document by ID: its markdown `content`, the `revision` to pass back as `baseRevision` when you edit it (synap_update_document), its top-level `sections` (id, owner ai|human, title — you may only rewrite `ai` ones), and `diagnostics` (embeds that will not render, each with a `fix`; null + diagnosticsError when they could not be checked). `format: "readable"` replaces every embed with its markdown fallback. Documents are long-form content (meeting notes, research, writeups, reports); get documentId from entity.documentId or search results.

| Parameter    | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------ | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `documentId` | string | yes      | Document UUID                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `format`     | enum   | no       | raw (default) = the stored markdown, embeds as directives (what you edit). readable = embeds replaced by their fallback text (what you quote or summarise). One of: `raw`, `readable`. |

## synap_list_proposals

**List proposals** · Group: `governance` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

List proposals — the audit trail of AI writes. AI writes return status 'proposed' when they require human approval — this is NOT an error. Filter by status: 'pending' (needs review), 'approved', 'rejected', 'auto_approved' (the write EXECUTED immediately under governance and filed this row as its receipt — use this to show the user what you did without asking), 'reverted', 'approval_failed', 'withdrawn', 'expired' (never decided — its session closed or its window lapsed). Pass sessionId to load the **session review pack** (proposals for one focus session). userId is auto-injected from the API key if not provided.

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `userId`      | string | no       | User ID (optional, auto-injected from API key if not provided)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `workspaceId` | string | no       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `sessionId`   | string | no       | Focus session UUID — list only proposals attributed to this session (the review pack).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `status`      | enum   | no       | One of: `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `auto_approved`, `reverted`, `approval_failed`, `withdrawn`, `expired`, `all`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `limit`       | number | no       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `detail`      | enum   | no       | 'summary' (default) returns one compact row per proposal — id, type, target, provenance, and a one-line summary — which is what a LIST is for. 'full' includes the entire `data` payload of every row: only ask for it when you need to inspect a specific proposal's contents, and pair it with a small `limit`. One of: `summary`, `full`. |

## synap_get_proposal

**Get proposal** · Group: `governance` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Read ONE proposal in full — the door for "why did my write not land?". Returns the row a reviewer sees: `status`, the whole `data` payload (the operations that would apply), `summary`, provenance, and — when an approve was attempted and FAILED (`status: 'approval_failed'`) — `rejectionReason` (the classified sentence) plus `data.failure` { errorClass, providerRef, missingFields }: the fields naming what to fix. Use it after a write comes back `proposed` and the user reports a problem approving it, then REPAIR the same proposal with synap_revise_proposal (never file a second one pointing at the first), or withdraw it with synap_reject_proposal. A proposal still `pending` after a failed approve attempt recorded nothing — read `data` and check the ops yourself. The raw upstream error text is deliberately NOT returned.

| Parameter    | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------ | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `proposalId` | string | yes      | Proposal UUID, as returned verbatim by synap_list_proposals or by the `proposalId` of a `proposed` write. A leading fragment of one also resolves, but pass the full id you were given. |

## synap_template_health

**Template health** · Group: `read` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

See where each workspace stands with its template — the pod's template-update radar. Per workspace: `drifted` (true = there is a step to take: a newer version, or a last update that did not finish); `state` (the last update: `active` done · `building` in progress · `awaiting-approval` its parts wait on the proposals in `awaitingApproval` · `partial`, `layer-2-not-run` or `failed` not finished); `applyWarning` (the pod's one sentence for what is left to do — relay it as is); `pendingDataChanges` (`{count, sentences, needsPodAdmin}` or null: the update changes existing data and waits for a PERSON to agree — never you; tell them what changes, in its sentences, and that they run `synap templates update <slug>` themselves, a pod owner or admin when `needsPodAdmin`); `updateProposal` (`{id}` or null: an update of this space is already proposed — point the person to that proposal, never file another); plus `installedVersion`, `latestVersion`, `warnings` and `lifecycle`: `current`, `retired` (`replacedBy` names the replacement, `retiredReason` says why; move it with `synap_retire_workspace`), `unlisted` (no longer in the catalog) or `unknown` (the catalog could not be fully read — never treat it as unlisted). The update path is `synap templates update <slug>`: run with an agent key it becomes a proposal the person approves, and data changes always need the person. Never re-apply a space that is `awaiting-approval` or has an `updateProposal`: the person's approval comes first. Read-only; scoped to the caller's own workspaces.

| Parameter     | Type    | Required | Description                                                                                                            |
| ------------- | ------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `driftedOnly` | boolean | no       | When true, return only workspaces with an available update (drifted). Default false = every workspace with its health. |

## synap_diagnose

**Diagnose** · Group: `read` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Understand what's happening / what's wrong — the pod's health door (the third door, alongside ask + capture). The MODE is derived from what you pass (never a tool name you choose): NO ARGS → whole-pod health (stuck runs, failed flows, review backlog + age, duplicate-proposal clusters, capability posture, agents hitting the daily cap) with a plain-language summary; `type` → a class as a surface (type:"proposal" = the review queue: pending count, oldest, duplicate clusters; type:"session" = stuck sessions; type:"agent" = agent roster + quality; type:"capability" = which installed verbs are turned on and which are not (a verb that is not turned on refuses to run); type:"run" = per-flow failure counts; type:"workspace" = the workspace landscape: per-workspace entity counts + which kinds live in each, PAIRWISE profile-slug overlap between workspaces, and flags for empty / duplicate-named / no-authored-identity workspaces — the "do I have too many workspaces?" read); `id` → auto-detects what the id is (proposal / session / capability / automation-run / playbook-run / agent / entity / view / document / workspace) and explains its state + WHY; `agentId` → an agent's behavioural scorecard (approve/reject/revise rates, top rejection reasons, duplicate rate, daily-cap posture). Backward-compatible: `runId`+`flowType` → that run's activity timeline (a capture's decision + trace events, each with a machine-readable reason + fixHint); `flowType`/`flowId` → the run feed. USER-scoped automatically.

| Parameter             | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `type`                | enum   | no       | Diagnose a whole CLASS as a surface (the review queue, stuck sessions, the agent roster, capability health, per-flow run failures, the workspace landscape). One of: `proposal`, `session`, `capability`, `agent`, `entity`, `run`, `workspace`. |
| `id`                  | string | no       | Any object id — the door auto-detects whether it is a proposal / session / capability / run / agent / entity / view / document / workspace and explains its state + why.                                                                         |
| `agentId`             | string | no       | An agent-user id → its behavioural quality scorecard (approve/reject/revise rates, rejection reasons, duplicate rate, daily-cap posture).                                                                                                        |
| `workspaceId`         | string | no       | Narrow whole-pod health or a class surface to ONE workspace lens (default: all workspaces you can see).                                                                                                                                          |
| `stuckThresholdHours` | number | no       | Override the 'stuck run' age boundary for whole-pod health (default 24h).                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `flowType`            | enum   | no       | Back-compat run-feed grammar: restrict to one ledger. REQUIRED when runId is given (the id space differs per flow). One of: `automation`, `playbook`, `capture`, `session`, `capability`.                                                        |
| `flowId`              | string | no       | Back-compat: restrict the feed to one flow's runs (automationId / playbookId).                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `runId`               | string | no       | Back-compat: a specific run id (or a capture's correlationId) → that run's activity timeline instead of the feed.                                                                                                                                |
| `limit`               | number | no       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## synap_get_entity

**Get entity** · Group: `read` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Get a single entity by ID with full details: all properties and metadata. Use after synap_ask to get complete data on a result. The id comes from synap_ask results or synap_create_entity responses.

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `entityId`    | string | yes      | Entity UUID                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `workspaceId` | string | no       | Workspace ID (optional)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `detail`      | enum   | no       | 'lean' (default) omits `effectivePropertiesByWorkspace` — the kind's property schema re-resolved once per accessible workspace, which is 83-93% of an entity read and long enough on its own to truncate the response. You still get the entity, its profile, its own workspace's `effectiveProperties` (the schema a write to this entity is validated against), facets, externalLinks and graph, plus a `propertyOverlays` signpost naming which workspaces differ. 'full' adds the per-workspace map back — ask for it only when you need to compare lenses. One of: `lean`, `full`. |

## synap_list_profiles

**List profiles** · Group: `read` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

List all available entity types (profiles) AND the relation types you may link them with. ALWAYS call at session start before creating entities or relations. Never assume 'deal', custom types or a relation slug exist — workspaces differ. Returns { profiles, relationTypes }: a lightweight digest per profile (id, slug, displayName, profileKind, entityScope, applicableKinds on roles, description ≤120 chars, workspaceId), and relationTypes as slugs grouped by lens ([{workspaceId:null, slugs}] = valid everywhere, plus per-workspace groups listing only the slugs that workspace adds). detail:'full' returns complete profile rows and full relation-type rows (displayName, description, isDirectional, inverseLabel). A relation `type` on synap_capture / synap_link_entities must be one of those slugs; any other slug is rejected with the valid list. If the relation read failed you get `relationTypesError` instead of `relationTypes`. Without a workspaceId, profiles are merged across your workspaces; a workspace whose profiles could not be read is named in `workspacesFailed` (its kinds are missing from `profiles`), never silently dropped. No property schemas here or in synap_orient. A kind's fields, enums and required keys: call synap_get_entity on any existing entity of that kind (its `effectiveProperties`); over HTTP, GET /api/hub/discover?profileSlugs=<slug>. For a kind with no entities yet, a write that breaks the schema is rejected with the valid fields quoted — fix and resend once.

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `workspaceId` | string | no       | Workspace ID (optional — omit to list across all workspaces)                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `detail`      | enum   | no       | Pass 'full' to receive complete profile rows (including renderer and uiHints columns) and full relation-type rows (displayName, description, isDirectional, inverseLabel). Omit for the lean digest (default): profile digests plus relation-type slugs grouped by lens. One of: `full`. |

## synap_get_relations

**Get relations** · Group: `read` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Get all relations for an entity — inbound and outbound. Returns typed edges with sourceEntityId, targetEntityId, and relation type. Dependencies ('blocks' / 'depends_on') are included: they are stored as one dependency link, so their row carries storedAs:'link' and a link id. Check before synap_link_entities to avoid duplicates. Use to understand an entity's connections.

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                      |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------- |
| `entityId`    | string | yes      | Entity UUID to get relations for |
| `workspaceId` | string | no       | Workspace ID (optional)          |

## synap_resolve_identity

**Resolve identity** · Group: `read` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Read-only identity PRE-CHECK — call BEFORE creating an entity to decide create-vs-enrich-vs-attach_facet. Pass the strong signals you have (email/phone/url/twitter/github/externalId) and/or a title + kindSlug. Returns match:'strong' (a globally-unique signal already resolves to an entity → do NOT create; enrich it or synap_attach_facet a new role onto entityId instead), match:'weak' (same-name candidates — advisory, inspect `candidates` before deciding), or match:'none' (safe to create). This is the dedup door: an entity exists ONCE (a person, a company); roles are facets, never second entities. Never writes.

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kindSlug`    | string | no       | The kind (profile slug) you intend to create, e.g. person, company. A same-name match must be this kind to count as a 'weak' match; cross-kind rows still appear in `candidates`. |
| `title`       | string | no       | The name/title to check. Omit to do a strong-signal-only lookup.                                                                                                                  |
| `signals`     | object | no       | Strong identity atoms you already know. Any one match auto-resolves.                                                                                                              |
| `properties`  | object | no       | Draft property bag — strong signals are also extracted from it (merged with `signals`).                                                                                           |
| `workspaceId` | string | no       | Workspace ID (optional).                                                                                                                                                          |

## synap_get_graph

**Get graph** · Group: `read` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Fetch ANY object PLUS everything it's linked to, typed. Returns { object, neighbors[], counts }. Each neighbor is { kind, subtype, name, id, edgeType, direction, via } — so you see a person linked to a deal, a skill linked to its tools, a session to its produced entities, etc. Graph by default: call this to understand an object's place in the pod before acting. Works for entity, project, view, channel, session, playbook, tool, skill, automation, document, track (a project's method: its project, sessions and playbook), proposal (what it governed and the session it was filed in) and run (an automation run: its automation and subject).

| Parameter | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                        |
| --------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`      | string | no       | The object's FULL uuid — short ids are not resolved by this tool. Provide id OR name.                                              |
| `name`    | string | no       | Fetch by NAME instead of id (a handle). Ambiguous names return candidates to pick from. Provide id OR name.                        |
| `type`    | string | no       | Object kind: entity (default), project, view, channel, session, playbook, tool, skill, automation, document, track, proposal, run. |
| `subtype` | string | no       | Narrow a name lookup (entity profileSlug, view type, tool/skill kind). Optional.                                                   |

## synap_create_entity

**Create entity** · Group: `data` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Create a SINGLE typed entity — no relations parameter exists here. Use when you already know the exact profileSlug + fields: the structured, deterministic sibling of synap_capture (which parses free text). Discover slugs with synap_list_profiles; synap_ask first to avoid duplicates. A same-kind record, or one of your own pending proposals, with the same name or identity does not block: the create is filed as a proposal and the person decides (keep both, use the existing one, fill its empty fields), so reuse the existing id when it is the same thing, and say in `reasoning` why a twin is separate. Placeholder person/company titles (e.g. 'Not publicly disclosed', 'unknown') are rejected. To create an entity TOGETHER WITH its edge to another entity in one reviewable unit, use synap_capture instead, passing both `entities` and `relations` — synap_link_entities cannot target an entity this call just proposed (its id isn't live until approved). A `decision` with `decisionStatus:'proposed'` ASKS the person automatically: pass `decisionOptions` (≤8 of {label, value?, description?}) + `recommendedOption`, and `sourceSessionId` to keep the question in your session; their answer updates it. Never create a decision for an answered confirm/choose — the pod already filed it (`slot.decisionId`).

| Parameter       | Type          | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------- | ------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `profileSlug`   | string        | yes      | Entity profile slug (e.g., note, task, event, person, contact, company, deal, bookmark, article). Use synap_list_profiles to discover available types. The cross-cutting container that spans workspaces is NOT an entity kind — it has its own door, synap_create_project.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `title`         | string        | yes      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `description`   | string        | no       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `content`       | string        | no       | LONG-FORM markdown body (the write-up itself, not a summary). Materialized into a versioned document linked to the entity — so a note/article/research entity and its body land in ONE call. Use `description` for a short preview and `content` for anything multi-paragraph; do NOT stuff long text into `properties`.                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `properties`    | object        | no       | Typed entity properties (profileSlug-specific fields)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `projectId`     | string        | no       | Optional project id to file the created entity into — stamps belongs_to_project membership.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `sessionId`     | string        | no       | OPTIONAL focus-session override. Leave it out and the write is attributed automatically — you do NOT normally pass this. Send it ONLY to disambiguate: when two or more of your focus sessions are open, automatic attribution deliberately declines rather than guess, and this is the only way to say which session the write belongs to. Also the way to JOIN a session another conversation started — automatic attribution never shares one across conversations. A session that isn't yours is ignored, not an error. |
| `facets`        | array<object> | no       | Kind + Facets: attach one or more role-profiles to the new entity in the SAME call (e.g. a person who is a client + investor). A role is a facet, NOT a separate entity — resolve identity first, then attach roles here. Each item: { slug, properties? }. Only applied when the entity is created (not when the create is proposal-gated).                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `expectedLabel` | string        | no       | The declared output slot this fulfils, exactly as declared on the session.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `reasoning`     | string        | no       | Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

## synap_update_entity

**Update entity** · Group: `data` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Update an entity's title, description, properties (JSONB), or long-form BODY (`content`). Requires entityId from search or synap_get_entity. May return 'proposed' if the write requires review. Use for property updates and status changes. To move a status (a kind's declared lifecycle), set the property to the new option AND pass `expectedStatus` = the status you read: `conflict` means someone moved it (re-read), a move into a done/lost option proposes, and a human-only option is refused. `content` REPLACES the whole body of the entity's linked document (an alias of synap_update_document with one replace_all op): it always goes to review, and it is refused if it changes a person's section or drops an embed. To change one section or one passage, use synap_update_document instead. If the entity has no body document yet the call is refused — create and attach one with synap_create_document({ entityId, title, content }). `documentId` attaches an EXISTING document from the entity's own space as the body (e.g. one left orphaned) and always goes to review (a document from another space is refused: the person attaches it); replacing a body the entity already has also needs `replaceBody: true`; undo puts the previous body back. `profileSlug` converts it to another kind, keeping its id and links (always reviewed).

| Parameter        | Type           | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | -------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `entityId`       | string         | yes      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `profileSlug`    | string         | no       | CONVERT the entity to another kind (e.g. a misfiled knowledge entry → decision, issue or note). It keeps its id, links, document and history; always a proposal. Send the new kind's required properties in `properties` in the same call. An unknown kind is refused — list kinds with synap_list_profiles.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `title`          | string         | no       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `description`    | string         | no       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `properties`     | object         | no       | Partial properties to merge into entity.properties JSONB                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `metadata`       | object         | no       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `content`        | string         | no       | Full REPLACEMENT body (markdown) for the entity's linked document — not a patch (for a patch: synap_update_document). Read the current body with synap_get_document first. Its outcome comes back under `body` and is always 'proposed'.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `expectedStatus` | string \| null | no       | When you change the status: the status you SAW (compare-and-set). If it moved meanwhile you get { status: 'conflict', conflict: { currentStatus } } and nothing is written — re-read and decide again; never retry blindly.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `documentId`     | string         | no       | Attach this EXISTING document (its id) as the entity's body — e.g. re-attach a document whose entity lost it. Not for new text: use `content` or synap_create_document.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `replaceBody`    | boolean        | no       | Set true with documentId when the entity ALREADY has a body and you mean to replace it (it is kept, detached, and comes back on undo). Without it the call is refused naming the current body. Always a proposal.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `reasoning`      | string         | no       | Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `sessionId`      | string         | no       | OPTIONAL focus-session override. Leave it out and the write is attributed automatically — you do NOT normally pass this. Send it ONLY to disambiguate: when two or more of your focus sessions are open, automatic attribution deliberately declines rather than guess, and this is the only way to say which session the write belongs to. Also the way to JOIN a session another conversation started — automatic attribution never shares one across conversations. A session that isn't yours is ignored, not an error. |

## synap_update_entities

**Update many entities** · Group: `data` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Change up to 500 existing entities in ONE call — retitles, property fixes, status moves. Use it for any change set; never script many single updates or Hub REST calls. Each item is {id, patch, expected?}; patch fields: title, description, properties, deleteProperties, expectedStatus (no kind change, no body — use synap_update_entity / synap_update_document for those). Governance is per item: each is written now (when it would auto-approve), or collected into ONE review for the person, or denied, or skipped (not found, changed since you read it, nothing to change). The answer lists applied, proposed {proposalId, count, reviewUrl}, denied, skipped, plus items[] with each verdict — a partial result is normal. 'proposed' is success: do not resend those items; a skipped item with `deferred: true` was kept on a space-join request and is replayed for you. Pass validate:true first to see the verdicts without writing. Pass an idempotencyKey so a retried call returns the first answer instead of acting twice.

| Parameter        | Type          | Required | Description                                                                    |
| ---------------- | ------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `items`          | array<object> | yes      |                                                                                |
| `validate`       | boolean       | no       | Dry run: return each item's verdict, write nothing.                            |
| `idempotencyKey` | string        | no       | 8–256 chars. The same key with the same items returns the first call's answer. |
| `reasoning`      | string        | no       | WHY these changes — shown to the person who reviews them. One line.            |

## synap_delete_entity

**Delete entity** · Group: `data` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Propose deleting an entity. For you, this is ALWAYS a proposal the person reviews — 'proposed' is success, never retry it. Nothing is removed until they approve; then the entity is hidden (soft delete), its body document is kept, and they can undo it. Use it to clean up what you created by mistake or what the person asked you to remove. To remove only a role, use synap_detach_facet; to change an entity, synap_update_entity.

| Parameter   | Type   | Required | Description                                                                            |
| ----------- | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `entityId`  | string | yes      | UUID of the entity to delete (from synap_ask, synap_find or synap_get_entity).         |
| `reasoning` | string | no       | Why it should go, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line. |

## synap_create_document

**Create document** · Group: `data` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Create a standalone document. TWO modes: (1) authored text — pass `content` (markdown) for meeting notes, research, plans that don't fit entity properties. (2) external reference — pass `url` (no `content`) to reference a file/page you have a LINK to but no bytes to upload (e.g. a Google Doc, a PDF URL); this is the agent-appropriate way to add a 'file' since an agent has no filesystem. Pass `entityId` to make it an existing entity's BODY: an entity has ONE body, so when it already has one the call is REFUSED before anything is written (`replaceBody: true` replaces it on purpose). A RELATED document is its own entity, linked with synap_link_entities. If you're also creating the entity, prefer synap_create_entity with `content` (entity + body in ONE call). To store real file bytes, use `synap_store_file` (≤10MB inline; bigger: `synap_request_upload`, then `synap_store_file({uploadToken})`). Attachment only happens when the document auto-approved; a proposal-gated one has no row to link yet, and the response says so.

| Parameter        | Type    | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | ------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idempotencyKey` | string  | no       | Optional: a stable key so a retry returns the PRIOR write, not a duplicate. Omit and identical content is deduped automatically; pass one to make a retry idempotent even if its content changed trivially.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `title`          | string  | yes      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `content`        | string  | no       | Authored document body (markdown or plain text). Mutually exclusive with `url`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `url`            | string  | no       | External reference: an https URL to a file/page you have a link to (no bytes stored). Use INSTEAD of `content` when referencing an existing file/link rather than authoring a body.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `entityId`       | string  | no       | Optional UUID of an EXISTING entity whose BODY this document becomes. The attach is a separate governed entity update — its own outcome comes back under `attached`. Refused when the entity already has a body (the refusal names it), unless `replaceBody` is true.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `replaceBody`    | boolean | no       | With `entityId`: replace the entity's existing body with this document on purpose. The old body document is kept but no longer attached. Omit to be refused instead.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `workspaceId`    | string  | no       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `sessionId`      | string  | no       | OPTIONAL focus-session override. Leave it out and the write is attributed automatically — you do NOT normally pass this. Send it ONLY to disambiguate: when two or more of your focus sessions are open, automatic attribution deliberately declines rather than guess, and this is the only way to say which session the write belongs to. Also the way to JOIN a session another conversation started — automatic attribution never shares one across conversations. A session that isn't yours is ignored, not an error. |
| `expectedLabel`  | string  | no       | The declared output slot this fulfils, exactly as declared on the session.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `reasoning`      | string  | no       | Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

## synap_update_document

**Update document** · Group: `data` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Edit a document with ops — a section, a passage, an addition — instead of rewriting it. Read it first with synap_get_document and pass its `revision` as `baseRevision`. Ops, applied in order: `upsert_section {id, title, body}` writes ONE `::::synap-section` block by id (replaces your own `ai` section, or appends a new one); `replace_text {old, new}` — `old` must match EXACTLY once, copy it from the document and include enough context (0 or 2+ matches is refused with the count); `append {body}`; `replace_all {content}` (whole body — needs baseRevision, always goes to review). Refused: changing a section whose owner is `human` (by any op), and removing an embed unless `allow_removing_embeds: true`. Usually returns 'proposed' (the person reviews a per-section before/after); a governance rule may apply it directly. The response carries `preview` and `diagnostics` (embeds that will not render, each with a `fix` — advisory, never a refusal). A 'changed after you read it' error means re-read and redraft.

| Parameter               | Type          | Required | Description                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------- | ------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `documentId`            | string        | yes      | Document UUID                                                                                                              |
| `baseRevision`          | number        | no       | The `revision` synap_get_document returned. The edit is refused if the document changed since.                             |
| `ops`                   | array<object> | yes      | The edits, applied in order.                                                                                               |
| `allow_removing_embeds` | boolean       | no       | Set true ONLY when removing an embed (synap-entity/view/cell) is the point of the edit; otherwise such an edit is refused. |
| `reasoning`             | string        | no       | Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line.                        |

## synap_request_upload

**Request upload** · Group: `data` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Get a URL to upload a file too large for `synap_store_file` inline (over 10MB, up to 500MB for video). Returns `{uploadUrl, headers, uploadToken, expiresAt, maxBytes}`: PUT the exact bytes to `uploadUrl` with exactly `headers` before `expiresAt`, then call `synap_store_file({uploadToken})` within the hour to save it. `size` must be the exact byte count.

| ------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `filename`    | string  | yes      | The file name (e.g. 'launch.mp4', 'deck.html').                                                                                      |
| `mimeType`    | string  | yes      | The content type (e.g. 'video/mp4', 'application/pdf'). Must be an allowed type.                                                     |
| `size`        | integer | yes      | Exact size of the file in bytes.                                                                                                     |
| `workspaceId` | string  | no       |                                                                                                                                      |
| `sessionId`   | string  | no       | OPTIONAL focus-session override, same rules as on `synap_store_file`. The upload's `synap_store_file` call defaults to this session. |

Use for a report/CSV/image/PDF/etc. you generated or hold. Pass `attachToEntityId` to attach it to an existing entity instead of creating a new file. For a link you have (no bytes), use `synap_create_document` with `url`. Max 10MB inline; for a bigger file call `synap_request_upload`, PUT the bytes, then call this with `uploadToken`.

Mutually exclusive with `content`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

Replaces `content`/`contentBase64`/`filename`/`mimeType`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `title`            | string | no       | Optional human-facing title (defaults to filename).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `workspaceId`      | string | no       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `attachToEntityId` | string | no       | Optional UUID of an EXISTING entity — attach the stored blob to it as provenance instead of creating a new `file` entity.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `sessionId`        | string | no       | OPTIONAL focus-session override. Leave it out and the write is attributed automatically — you do NOT normally pass this. Send it ONLY to disambiguate: when two or more of your focus sessions are open, automatic attribution deliberately declines rather than guess, and this is the only way to say which session the write belongs to. Also the way to JOIN a session another conversation started — automatic attribution never shares one across conversations. A session that isn't yours is ignored, not an error. |
| `expectedLabel`    | string | no       | The declared output slot this fulfils, exactly as declared on the session.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## synap_remember_fact

**Remember fact** · Group: `data` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Store a durable fact about the user (preference, habit, working style, technical context) as a governed `user_observation`. Returns status:"proposed" with a `reviewUrl` when the fact is your own inference — that is normal, not an error — or status:"created" when you pass userStated:true because the user told you directly. Returns the record's id so you can link or revert it.

| Parameter        | Type    | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idempotencyKey` | string  | no       | Optional: a stable key so a retry returns the PRIOR write, not a duplicate. Omit and identical content is deduped automatically; pass one to make a retry idempotent even if its content changed trivially. |
| `userId`         | string  | no       | User ID (auto-injected from API key if not provided)                                                                                                                                                        |
| `fact`           | string  | yes      | The fact to remember                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `confidence`     | number  | no       | How sure you are, 0–1 (default 0.8). Stored on the observation; it does NOT change the governance outcome.                                                                                                  |
| `category`       | enum    | no       | Which bucket the observation belongs to (default 'preferences'). One of: `working_style`, `communication`, `focus`, `preferences`, `habits`, `technical`.                                                   |
| `userStated`     | boolean | no       | true ONLY if the user directly stated this; do not infer. This is the single signal that makes the write auto-approve instead of proposing.                                                                 |

## synap_link_entities

**Link entities** · Group: `data` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Create a typed relation between two entities. `type` is NOT a free string: it must name an existing relation-def slug — real ones include 'relates_to', 'references', 'mentions', 'parent_of', 'depends_on', 'blocks', 'created_by', 'works_at'. To file an entity into a project use synap_file_into_project — `belongs_to_project` is refused here. The default slugs resolve pod-wide, so no `workspaceId` is needed for them; a workspace may add or override slugs. A slug that names no relation def is rejected. If available to you, check this entity's existing relations first to avoid duplicates. Both endpoints must already be LIVE entities — an id from a still-pending synap_create_entity proposal will fail; to create an entity and its edge together, use synap_capture with `entities` + `relations` instead. May return 'proposed'. Builds the knowledge graph.

| Parameter        | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                          |
| ---------------- | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sourceEntityId` | string | yes      | Source entity UUID                                                                                                   |
| `targetEntityId` | string | yes      | Target entity UUID                                                                                                   |
| `type`           | string | no       | Relation type — an existing relation-def slug (e.g. 'relates_to', 'references', 'mentions', 'parent_of', 'works_at') |
| `workspaceId`    | string | no       | Workspace ID (optional)                                                                                              |
| `reasoning`      | string | no       | Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line.                  |

## synap_attach_facet

**Attach facet** · Group: `data` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Attach a ROLE to an existing entity (Kind + Facets). A role — client, partner, prospect, investor, sponsor — is a FACET, never its own entity: an entity IS one kind (person, company) and HAS many roles. Resolve identity FIRST (synap_ask / synap_get_entities on strong signals like email / phone / website) so you attach the role to the REAL entity instead of creating a duplicate. Governed like any write: may return 'proposed' (a proposalId to review) — NEVER treat that as an error. Use synap_list_profiles to find role slugs (profileKind='role') and which kinds they apply to (applicableKinds).

| Parameter         | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `entityId`        | string | yes      | UUID of the entity to attach the role to.                                                                      |
| `facetSlug`       | string | yes      | Role-profile slug to attach (profileKind='role', e.g. 'client').                                               |
| `properties`      | object | no       | Optional facet-specific properties.                                                                            |
| `workspaceId`     | string | no       | Optional facet visibility lens. Omit to inherit the parent entity's workspace.                                 |
| `contextEntityId` | string | no       | Optional disambiguator when the same role attaches in multiple contexts (e.g. a client OF a specific company). |
| `reasoning`       | string | no       | Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line.            |

## synap_detach_facet

**Detach facet** · Group: `data` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Detach (soft-delete) a role from an entity (Kind + Facets). Provide the entityId + facetSlug of the role to remove (or a facetId directly). Governed like any write: may return 'proposed' — NEVER treat that as an error. Removing a role never deletes the entity; only the role-facet is retired.

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                         |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `entityId`    | string | no       | UUID of the entity carrying the role (with facetSlug).                                              |
| `facetSlug`   | string | no       | Role-profile slug to detach from the entity (paired with entityId).                                 |
| `facetId`     | string | no       | Alternative to entityId+facetSlug: the facet's own UUID (the handle synap_attach_facet returns).    |
| `workspaceId` | string | no       | Optional workspace lens used to resolve the facet when detaching by entityId + facetSlug.           |
| `reasoning`   | string | no       | Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line. |

## synap_define_role

**Define role type** · Group: `schema` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Define or WIDEN a role (facet): a hat on ANY entity kind, not only person/company. Example: applicableKinds ['item'] means 'this item is an X'. Call ONLY after synap_list_profiles. If the slug already exists, extra applicableKinds are MERGED (widen only — never a second slug for the same hat). Prefer attach_facet; widen when kind_mismatch. NULL stored allowlist = any kind. Governed: may return 'proposed' — NEVER treat that as an error.

| Parameter         | Type          | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------- | ------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `slug`            | string        | yes      | URL-safe role slug (lowercase, digits, hyphens), e.g. 'market-maker'.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `displayName`     | string        | yes      | Human-readable role name, e.g. 'Market Maker'.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `applicableKinds` | array<string> | no       | Kind slugs this hat can attach to (item, person, company, task, …). Merged on an existing role. Defaults to ['company','person'] only when omitted on CREATE — that default is a convenience, not a model limit.                            |
| `description`     | string        | no       | Optional description of what the role represents.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `icon`            | string        | no       | Optional icon hint for the role.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `roleCategory`    | string        | no       | Optional grouping key so an automation can select entities wearing ANY role in this category via entity.query { roleCategory } — e.g. tag every supply role 'provider'. Future roles tagged the same category qualify with no query change. |
| `properties`      | object        | no       | Optional default property values for facets of this role.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `workspaceId`     | string        | yes      | Workspace to define the role in.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `reasoning`       | string        | no       | Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line.                                                                                                                                         |

## synap_define_kind

**Define entity kind** · Group: `schema` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Define a new entity KIND — AND the door for ADDING A FIELD to a kind that already exists. It is SLUG-IDEMPOTENT: re-call it with an EXISTING slug and it returns that profile and adds only the `properties[]` that are not there yet (an existing field reports status 'unchanged' and is never rewritten).
