## synap_match_playbooks

**Match templates** · Group: `build` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Suggest playbooks for what the user wants — text-first, suggest-and-confirm, NEVER auto-run the top hit. Pass intentText (what they said — that exact spelling) and/or profileSlug (the kind of thing, e.g. 'post') and/or entityId. At least ONE is required: a call with no signal is REFUSED (without one, every active playbook ties at the same score; to just see what exists, call synap_list_playbooks). Read-only. Returns ranked candidates best first ({ id, name, scope, templateKind, goalTemplate, subjectProfileSlug, params, executor, score, reason, signals }); [] when none. `scope: 'project'` (templateKind 'Track template') is a method a project runs as a TRACK — start it with synap_start_track; `'session'` ('Work template') is one working session. Pass projectId (or name the project/track in intentText) and a track template ranks above its same-name session twin. Show the reason when you suggest; wait for confirmation before launching via synap_run_playbook (or, on doors that expose sessions, by opening the template as a working session with the chosen entity as its subject). Each of your words is weighted by how rare it is among the candidates, so a specific word outranks one most playbooks share. A playbook is returned only with a reason about THIS request (one of your words, the entity's kind, or one of its roles): a playbook with no subject (e.g. Plan Next Content) comes back only when your words match it. When profileSlug is omitted, every active visible playbook is a candidate.

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `profileSlug` | string | no       | Optional entity profile slug to match against (e.g. 'post', 'deal', 'lead', 'competitor'). Omit to search all active visible playbooks by intentText alone.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `entityId`    | string | no       | Optional UUID of the specific entity — round-trip it as the launch's subject once a playbook is chosen. Widens the match with that entity's live facet-role slugs.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `workspaceId` | string | no       | Workspace ID to scope the lookup (optional — falls back to the user's first workspace). Pod-wide playbooks match regardless.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `intentText`  | string | no       | What the user said they want. Sufficient on its own — ranks the candidates and each result carries `score` and a human-readable `reason`. A kind or role match is returned without a word match; a playbook with no subject needs one. Show the reason when you suggest a playbook; never run one without the user's confirmation. |
| `projectId`   | string | no       | Optional project you are working in. Never filters — it ranks a track template (scope project) above its same-name session twin.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

## synap_create_playbook

**Create template** · Group: `build` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Create a reusable playbook (staged process/session template) for a repeatable workflow — discoverable via synap_list_playbooks, launched via synap_run_playbook. goalTemplate may reference a declared param as {name} — a playbook run fills it; an undeclared name, or {{name}}, is refused. The default scope "session" is a template for one focus session; scope "project" (a staged method a track runs) is LEGACY — a new track needs none. Declare params to make the method self-onboarding: required params become questions for the person when the track starts. A PROCESS on a kind or role: set subjectProfileSlug; it FOLLOWS the lifecycle the profile declares (omit statusProperty, or name that same property — never a second status field). Give each stage the subjectStatus it moves the thing to (an existing option), gates at the commitments, onFail loops, typed expectedOutputs, plus workers (activators: on, size, mode) — load_skill system/synap/processes (model: system/synap/work-model) first. An agent call ALWAYS lands as a proposal: status="proposed" is SUCCESS — say it is awaiting review, pass on reviewUrl, do not retry. Creates it on this pod only; an official template is written in the catalog and published with `synap catalog publish --official`.

| Parameter            | Type          | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------- | ------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`               | string        | yes      | Playbook display name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `goalTemplate`       | string        | yes      | The session goal this playbook instantiates (e.g. 'Analyze competitors for {market}', with market declared in params). Reference a param as {name}, never {{name}}.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `description`        | string        | no       | What this playbook is for.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `stages`             | array<object> | no       | Ordered stages. Each: { key, name, category, description?, goal?, suggestedTasks?, position?, indefinite?, subjectStatus?, gate?, onFail?, expectedOutputs?, criteria? }. `category` is REQUIRED — it is the closed rollup axis a cross-playbook board groups on, since your stage `key`s are this playbook's own vocabulary and no other playbook shares them. Stage keys must be unique within the playbook.                                                                                                              |
| `status`             | enum          | no       | Defaults to 'active' (immediately runnable). One of: `draft`, `active`, `paused`, `archived`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `workspaceId`        | string        | no       | Home workspace (optional — falls back to the user's first workspace).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `subjectProfileSlug` | string        | no       | Slug of the kind or role this playbook runs ON (e.g. 'crm-lead'), so synap_match_playbooks can offer it for that kind. A slug that resolves to no profile is refused — define the kind first.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `statusProperty`     | string        | no       | Slug of the subject's lifecycle property (e.g. 'post-status'). Omit it: the process follows the lifecycle the kind or role declares. If you name it, name that same property. Needs subjectProfileSlug.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `activators`         | array<object> | no       | Workers: when the process starts on its subject: [{ on: 'created' \| 'enters_status' \| 'count' (status+min, one run over the set) \| 'schedule' (cron) \| 'manual', status?, size?: 'per_thing' (default) \| 'per_moment' (count/schedule always are), mode: 'propose' (default) \| 'run', maxPendingApprovals? (default 20, throttles) }]. `run` only when cheap and safe. Needs subjectProfileSlug; compiled to a governed rule the owner can pause, fired once per thing per transition.                                |
| `humanOnlyStatuses`  | array<string> | no       | LEGACY coverage: status options no stage owns, set only by a person (e.g. Idea, Archived). The lifecycle's own humanOnly flag is what the status door enforces; with the stages' subjectStatus values this list should cover every option.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `expectedOutputs`    | array<object> | no       | What every run of this playbook must produce (playbook-level slots): each { kind, label, relationToSubject? }.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `scope`              | enum          | no       | What the playbook instantiates. 'session' (default): a template for ONE bounded focus session, which a session or a worker follows. 'project': LEGACY — a staged method a track runs (synap_start_track); a new track needs none. One of: `session`, `project`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `params`             | array<object> | no       | What the method needs to know. A required param left unanswered when synap_start_track runs becomes a question owed to the person (answer later with synap_set_track_params); optional ones fall back to their default.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `criteria`           | array<object> | no       | Binary acceptance criteria every session of this playbook is graded against. Each: { key (lowercase slug), statement, required?, check: { kind: evidence\|capability\|judge\|human, capability? (kind 'capability'), evidenceKey? (kind 'evidence'), hint? }, stageKey? }.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `sessionId`          | string        | no       | OPTIONAL focus-session override. Leave it out and the write is attributed automatically — you do NOT normally pass this. Send it ONLY to disambiguate: when two or more of your focus sessions are open, automatic attribution deliberately declines rather than guess, and this is the only way to say which session the write belongs to. Also the way to JOIN a session another conversation started — automatic attribution never shares one across conversations. A session that isn't yours is ignored, not an error. |

## synap_update_playbook

**Update template** · Group: `build` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Edit an EXISTING playbook's definition: pass `playbookId` (from synap_list_playbooks) and ONLY the fields to change — an absent field stays as it is; a list you pass (stages, params, criteria, expectedOutputs, activators) REPLACES the stored one. To change a playbook proposal that is still PENDING, revise it with synap_revise_proposal (patch {kind:'inner', fields}) instead. Edits it on this pod only; an official template is changed in the catalog.

| Parameter            | Type          | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------- | ------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `playbookId`         | string        | yes      | The playbook to edit (id from synap_list_playbooks).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `name`               | string        | no       | New display name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `goalTemplate`       | string        | no       | New session goal. Reference a param as {name} (declared in params, the stored ones or the ones you pass), never {{name}}.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `description`        | string        | no       | What this playbook is for.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `stages`             | array<object> | no       | Ordered stages. Each: { key, name, category, description?, goal?, suggestedTasks?, position?, indefinite?, subjectStatus?, gate?, onFail?, expectedOutputs?, criteria? }. `category` is REQUIRED — it is the closed rollup axis a cross-playbook board groups on, since your stage `key`s are this playbook's own vocabulary and no other playbook shares them. Stage keys must be unique within the playbook.                                                                                                              |
| `params`             | array<object> | no       | What the method needs to know. A required param left unanswered when synap_start_track runs becomes a question owed to the person (answer later with synap_set_track_params); optional ones fall back to their default.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `criteria`           | array<object> | no       | Binary acceptance criteria every session of this playbook is graded against. Each: { key (lowercase slug), statement, required?, check: { kind: evidence\|capability\|judge\|human, capability? (kind 'capability'), evidenceKey? (kind 'evidence'), hint? }, stageKey? }.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `subjectProfileSlug` | string        | no       | Repoint the kind or role this playbook runs ON. A slug that resolves to no profile is refused.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `statusProperty`     | string        | no       | Slug of the subject's lifecycle property (e.g. 'post-status'). Omit it: the process follows the lifecycle the kind or role declares. If you name it, name that same property. Needs subjectProfileSlug.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `activators`         | array<object> | no       | Workers: when the process starts on its subject: [{ on: 'created' \| 'enters_status' \| 'count' (status+min, one run over the set) \| 'schedule' (cron) \| 'manual', status?, size?: 'per_thing' (default) \| 'per_moment' (count/schedule always are), mode: 'propose' (default) \| 'run', maxPendingApprovals? (default 20, throttles) }]. `run` only when cheap and safe. Needs subjectProfileSlug; compiled to a governed rule the owner can pause, fired once per thing per transition.                                |
| `humanOnlyStatuses`  | array<string> | no       | LEGACY coverage: status options no stage owns, set only by a person (e.g. Idea, Archived). The lifecycle's own humanOnly flag is what the status door enforces; with the stages' subjectStatus values this list should cover every option.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `expectedOutputs`    | array<object> | no       | What every run of this playbook must produce (playbook-level slots): each { kind, label, relationToSubject? }.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `status`             | enum          | no       | Lifecycle of the template itself (not of its subject). One of: `draft`, `active`, `paused`, `archived`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `scope`              | enum          | no       | What the playbook instantiates. 'session': a template for ONE bounded focus session. 'project': LEGACY — a staged method a track runs. One of: `session`, `project`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `reasoning`          | string        | no       | Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `sessionId`          | string        | no       | OPTIONAL focus-session override. Leave it out and the write is attributed automatically — you do NOT normally pass this. Send it ONLY to disambiguate: when two or more of your focus sessions are open, automatic attribution deliberately declines rather than guess, and this is the only way to say which session the write belongs to. Also the way to JOIN a session another conversation started — automatic attribution never shares one across conversations. A session that isn't yours is ignored, not an error. |

## synap_governance

**Get governance policy** · Group: `governance` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Read workspace governance policy and count of pending proposals. Use before writes to understand auto-approve rules and whether proposals will be created. When called with an agent key it also returns `agentBudget`: YOUR pending-proposal cap, how many of it you are using, whether you are BLOCKED (at the cap your writes are refused — nothing is written), and the remedy, including the link to a cap-raise request already waiting for your owner's review. Read-only: it never files anything.

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description    |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | -------------- |
| `workspaceId` | string | yes      | Workspace UUID |

## synap_set_workspace_focus

**Set space focus** · Group: `spaces` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Pin your runtime workspace focus so every subsequent write (create/update/capture) with no explicit workspaceId lands there — the 'use the CRM workspace until I say otherwise' scenario. ADVISORY: a call that DOES pass an explicit workspaceId still overrides the focus; reads are unaffected. Sticky in THIS conversation until cleared — another conversation keeps its own (set the same focus there to share it); the reply's `focusScope` says which. Pass `workspace` as a name (matched against your workspaces) or an id; omit it (or pass 'none'/'clear') to clear the focus. Pinning a space also RETURNS its `brief` (purpose, the kinds it holds, its skills, its playbooks) — the same brief a pinned `synap_orient` serves, so focusing is also how you learn what the space knows before you work in it.

| Parameter   | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `workspace` | string | no       | Workspace name or id to focus on. Omit, or pass 'none'/'clear', to clear the current focus. |

## synap_set_project_focus

**Set project focus** · Group: `spaces` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

DECLARE which project you are working on, so writes that don't pin their own project file into it — the 'everything I do now is for the Apollo migration' scenario. Sticky in THIS conversation until cleared — another conversation keeps its own (set the same focus there to share it); the reply's `focusScope` says which. A call that passes an explicit projectId still wins. Filing into a project GRANTS ACCESS to it, so this is a DECLARATION only: the project is verified to exist and be visible to you at set time, and nothing infers a project from what you write. Pass `project` as a name (matched against the projects you can see) or an id; omit it (or pass 'none'/'clear') to clear the focus.

| Parameter | Type   | Required | Description                                                                              |
| --------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `project` | string | no       | Project name or id to declare. Omit, or pass 'none'/'clear', to clear the current focus. |

## synap_organize_library

**Organize Library** · Group: `data` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Propose how to ORGANISE the person's Library (the links, files and notes they kept) — never add to it: your own words, links and files go to synap_capture. Without `ops`: returns the Library's groups (id, name, note, item counts) so you can name one. With `ops`: files ONE proposal for the person's review — always a proposal for an agent, `proposed` is success (surface reviewUrl); nothing changes until they approve, then it applies exactly as if they had done it. Ops: group.create {name, note?, itemIds?} · group.items {groupId, add?, remove?} (existing items) · group.update {groupId, name?, note?, workspaceId?: the space Build files into, null clears} · group.build {groupId} (approval runs Build, whose result is reviewed again). Item ids come from synap_ask (its Library hits carry their id). An id that is not in this Library is refused.

| Parameter   | Type          | Required | Description                                                                           |
| ----------- | ------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ops`       | array<object> | no       | 1-50 organisation ops, applied in order on approval. Omit to list the groups.         |
| `reasoning` | string        | no       | Why this organisation helps, in the person's words — shown to the reviewer. One line. |

## synap_capture

**Capture** · Group: `entry` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

THE write door — everything worth remembering goes through here, in whatever shape you already have it. Never classify your input first: the payload is a GRADIENT, and you send as much structure as you have.
• `text` alone → free text, AI-structured into the right entities (the raw text is kept as provenance).
• `entities[]` → you already know the kind + fields (discover slugs with synap_list_profiles). `ref` is optional for a single entity.
• `entities[]` + `relations[]` → a graph. Refs let you link things that don't exist yet; the whole graph is ONE reviewable proposal, so nothing half-lands. To link something that already exists, give it a `ref` plus `existingEntityId`.
• + `projects[]` / `sessions[]` / `documents[]` / `links[]` → a CONNECTED PLAN: build a project, its sessions (parent = `parentRef`, dependencies = `blockedByRefs`, or edges in `links[]`), a spec document and the entities they are about — ONE reviewable proposal, refs across all of it, applied ALL-OR-NONE on approval. Reference plan items by REF; ids exist only after approval (the receipt lists each step with `id: null`; once applied, `synap_list_proposals` shows `materializedIds` ref → id). To change the plan, revise it (full updated operations, re-validated by the pod) — never file a second proposal that points at pending items.
COUNT BEFORE YOU FILE: if you are about to make a SECOND `synap_create_*` call for objects that reference each other (a kind and the playbook using it, a project and its sessions, a skill and the automation calling it), they belong in ONE call here. N connected objects as N proposals exhausts your pending-proposal cap, and re-sending a capped write through another door is how the same playbook lands in the pod twice. Give each `sessions[]` step its `expectedOutputs` — the plan's object list IS the definition of done, so the person can see what is still owed instead of being told a percentage.
PLAN EXAMPLE — a project, a root session with two children (one blocked by the other), a spec document:
{ "entities": [ { "ref": "acme", "profileSlug": "company", "title": "Acme Corp", "properties": { "website": "https://acme.com" } } ], "projects": [ { "ref": "p1", "name": "Acme onboarding", "subjectRef": "acme", "evidenceRefs": ["acme"] } ], "sessions": [ { "ref": "s0", "title": "Onboard Acme", "goal": "Acme is live on the platform", "projectRef": "p1", "subjectRef": "acme" }, { "ref": "s1", "title": "Write the spec", "goal": "Spec signed off by Acme", "parentRef": "s0", "projectRef": "p1" }, { "ref": "s2", "title": "Build the import", "goal": "Acme data imported", "parentRef": "s0", "projectRef": "p1", "blockedByRefs": ["s1"] } ], "documents": [ { "ref": "spec", "title": "Acme onboarding spec", "content": "# Spec\n…", "sessionRef": "s1" } ] }
Call it AFTER learning something durable — don't wait to be asked. Placement uses EXISTING lenses only; capture never invents a workspace. `global:true` stores a pod-wide runbook (text only).
DEDUP: the strong identity signals are the property keys `email`, `phone`, `website`, `linkedinUrl`, `twitterHandle`, `githubUsername` — those exact spellings. Sending a URL under any other key (e.g. `url`) is NOT a dedup signal and will duplicate the entity.

EXAMPLE 1 — raw text:
{ "text": "Met Ada Lovelace of Acme at the conference — she owns their data platform and wants a demo in March." }

EXAMPLE 2 — one structured entity, with properties + a long body:
{ "entities": [ { "profileSlug": "person", "title": "Ada Lovelace", "properties": { "email": "ada@acme.com", "role": "Head of Data" }, "content": "## Notes\nOwns the data platform. Wants a March demo." } ] }

EXAMPLE 3 — a small graph (refs link entities that do not exist yet):
{ "entities": [ { "ref": "p1", "profileSlug": "person", "title": "Ada Lovelace", "properties": { "email": "ada@acme.com" } }, { "ref": "c1", "profileSlug": "company", "title": "Acme Corp", "properties": { "website": "https://acme.com" } } ], "relations": [ { "sourceRef": "p1", "targetRef": "c1", "type": "works_at" } ] }

ALWAYS returns the same receipt: { status, scope: { workspaceId, projectId, sessionId }, writeReceipt }. `status: "proposed"` is SUCCESS, not an error — writeReceipt.reviewUrl is a real clickable link and you MUST surface it as a markdown link in your reply, e.g. "Queued that for your review: [Review proposal](reviewUrl)" — never report a proposed write as simply done, and never withhold the link.
`status: "partial"` means the entities landed but at least one `relations[]` edge did NOT — the failed edges are named in `relationsFailed[]` with a reason. Do not report a partial capture as done: say which edges did not land. The usual cause is a `type` that names no relation def — re-send those edges with a real slug. The default slugs resolve pod-wide: a capture needs no `workspaceId` for its edges to land.
THE DOOR MAY REJECT, and a rejection is a CORRECT outcome — do not retry it: `status: "rejected"` with reason "already-known" (a lone entity carrying nothing but identity signals that already resolve to an existing one — its id is returned; re-send with content / extra properties / relations to ENRICH it instead), "no-durable-content" (nothing storable was sent). When the AI structurer is DOWN the text lane no longer rejects — it saves your text as a plain unstructured note and returns `degraded: true` with a `degradedNotice`: the note LANDED, but it is NOT the person/task/decision it describes, so relay that notice to the user instead of reporting a normal capture.

| Parameter          | Type          | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------ | ------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text`             | string        | no       | Free-form text to parse (max 8000 chars). Send this when you have prose. If you ALSO send `entities[]`, the structured payload is used and this text is kept on the proposal as provenance.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `entities`         | array<object> | no       | Structured payload: the things to write. Each needs a `profileSlug`; `ref` is only required when a relation points at it (it is auto-assigned otherwise).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `relations`        | array<object> | no       | The graph's edges (needs `entities[]`). Both refs MUST name entities in this same call.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `projects`         | array<object> | no       | PLAN: projects to create. `ref` is how sessions/entities point at it (`projectRef`). An agent-proposed project needs ≥5 evidence entities (`evidenceRefs` of entities in this call + `evidenceEntityIds` you can see); below that the step is still filed, MARKED for the reviewer, and never auto-applies.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `sessions`         | array<object> | no       | PLAN: focus sessions to open. Each `…Ref` names a step in this call; its `…Id` twin names something that already exists (never both). Parent = the spawned_from edge (a parent never auto-closes).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `documents`        | array<object> | no       | PLAN: documents to create (markdown). Attach one as an entity's body (`entityRef`/`entityId`) and/or record it as a session's output (`sessionRef`/`sessionId`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `links`            | array<object> | no       | PLAN: session edges. `blocked_by`: from waits on to. `spawned_from`: to is from's parent (from must be a session in this call). Cycles are refused.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `skills`           | array<object> | no       | RULE LOOP: instruction skills to create — the FACT half, what an agent should KNOW while reasoning. `ref` is how a `rules[]` step points at it (`factRef`). This is an instruction, NOT a capability/verb: it does not install a tool.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `automations`      | array<object> | no       | RULE LOOP: automations to create — the BEHAVIOUR half, what RUNS when the world changes. `ref` is how a `rules[]` step points at it (`behaviourRefs`). ALWAYS materialized DISABLED (draft): approving the proposal creates it, it never arrives already running — switch it on yourself afterwards. A flow node may name a skill THIS SAME call creates: skills are applied before automations, so the reference resolves.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `rules`            | array<object> | no       | RULE LOOP: the memory that joins a FACT to a BEHAVIOUR. Needs `factRef` and/or `behaviourRefs` — each names a `skills[]` / `automations[]` step in this call, or a real UUID that already exists. A rule joined to nothing is refused.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `summary`          | string        | no       | One line the reviewer sees on the proposal card (structured payloads). Auto-generated when omitted — write your own, it is what the user reads.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `validate`         | boolean       | no       | Dry run for the structured `entities[]` lane: run the capture's validators and write NOTHING. Returns `dryRun: true` and `status: "valid"` or `"invalid"`, with every problem at once: ref and shape problems in `problems[]`, unknown relation slugs in `relationsFailed[]` (same shape as a real call, with the valid slugs named), and unknown profiles or invalid properties in `invalidEntities[]`. `notChecked[]` lists what only the real write can decide. Not supported on the `text` lane.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `profileSlug`      | string        | no       | Optional kind hint for the work lane. It guides extraction, and if AI structuring is unavailable the text is still saved as this kind (marked degraded) when it is a kind in your lens; otherwise as a note.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `global`           | boolean       | no       | GLOBAL lane: store as a pod-wide procedural runbook (knowledge_keys) instead of structuring into entities. Use for cross-project how-to / decisions / operational docs ('how we deploy', 'auth works like…'). Mirrors the CLI's `capture --global`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `key`              | string        | no       | Optional stable key (namespace:slug, e.g. 'deploy:backend') for a global runbook — derived from the text if omitted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `workspaceId`      | string        | no       | Explicit workspace pin (rung-1 placement) — wins over ontology/session/relational routing and the AI's workspace guess. Pass this when you already know exactly which workspace the capture belongs in, and to ACT on a previous call's `pendingWorkspaceSwitch` (the AI's suggestion is never applied on its own — a pin that differs from it is recorded as the suggestion being corrected). Leave it out to let the resolver place it (see `workspaceRouting`). An `entities[]` graph with no `workspaceId` is placed only when every entity's kind (and roles) points at the same space; otherwise it stays pod-wide and returns `placement` (reason + candidates) and, when there is a candidate, `pendingWorkspaceSwitch`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `projectId`        | string        | no       | Optional project id to file the created entities into — stamps belongs_to_project membership.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `projectName`      | string        | no       | Instead of projectId: the exact name of one of your projects. A name that matches none of them refuses the whole capture (nothing is filed) and names the closest projects with their ids — re-send with projectId.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `dedupMode`        | enum          | no       | Dedup strategy for surfaced candidates: 'title' = string-similarity search only, 'semantic' = pgvector cosine search over entity embeddings (catches paraphrases with no shared words), 'both' (default) = run both and keep the strongest match per entity. One of: `title`, `semantic`, `both`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `workspaceRouting` | enum          | no       | How much latitude the backend resolver has over the AI's workspace GUESS (rung 5) specifically — it does NOT gate the deterministic rungs above it (ontology role-routing, focus-session context, relational gravity), which still run and place the capture regardless of this setting. An AI guess NEVER moves a capture through this door, in any mode: 'auto' and 'ask' now do the SAME thing — the capture stays where it would have landed and the guess comes back as `pendingWorkspaceSwitch` ({ suggestedWorkspaceId, suggestedWorkspaceName, reason, confidence }) for you to confirm with the user; there is no `movedToWorkspace` on the response any more. To ACT on a suggestion, re-call synap_capture with `workspaceId` set to `pendingWorkspaceSwitch.suggestedWorkspaceId` (that pin is recorded as the user accepting it). 'locked' = suppress the AI guess entirely, so no suggestion is returned; it does NOT freeze the capture onto the caller's/session workspace by itself. To pin an EXACT workspace and skip resolution altogether (deterministic rungs included), pass an explicit `workspaceId` (rung-1 placement) instead of relying on this setting. One of: `auto`, `ask`, `locked`. |
| `sessionId`        | string        | no       | OPTIONAL focus-session override. Leave it out and the write is attributed automatically — you do NOT normally pass this. Send it ONLY to disambiguate: when two or more of your focus sessions are open, automatic attribution deliberately declines rather than guess (mis-grouping a write is worse than not grouping it), and this is the only way to say which session the write belongs to. Also the way to JOIN a session another conversation started — automatic attribution never shares one across conversations. A session that isn't yours is ignored, not an error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

## synap_create_workspace

**Create space** · Group: `spaces` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Escalation L3 (governed — may propose): create a workspace from a definition. Template-first: market.search(kind:template) + prefer install before freehand create. Only after workspace-design four conditions hold and no template fits. Capture never invents a workspace. Pass stable proposalId for idempotency. Creates it on this pod only; an official template is written in the catalog and published with `synap catalog publish --official`.

| Parameter    | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                         |
| ------------ | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`       | string | yes      | Workspace display name                                                                              |
| `definition` | object | no       | Optional WorkspaceProposal definition fields                                                        |
| `proposalId` | string | no       | Idempotency key (optional)                                                                          |
| `reasoning`  | string | no       | Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line. |

## synap_declare_workspace_source

**Declare space source edge** · Group: `spaces` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Declare a cross-workspace DATA EDGE on an EXISTING workspace by setting/merging its edge fields. `sourceRoles` = per-domain role this workspace plays (provider | consumer | provider-consumer), e.g. Marketing consumes Comms → { comms: 'consumer' }. `defaultSources` = per-domain the workspace to READ that domain from (the source of truth), e.g. { comms: { workspaceId: '<comms-ws-id>' } }. MERGES per-domain — existing domains and all other settings are preserved, never clobbered. Use this to wire the enterprise graph (provides/consumes) instead of copying data between workspaces. Editor+ membership required.

| Parameter        | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `workspaceId`    | string | yes      | The workspace to declare the edge ON (the subject).                                                                                                                                                          |
| `sourceRoles`    | object | no       | Domain → role map. Values: 'provider' \| 'consumer' \| 'provider-consumer'. Example: { "comms": "consumer" }. Merged per-domain into the existing map.                                                       |
| `defaultSources` | object | no       | Domain → default source workspace to read that domain from. Each value: { workspaceId (required), capability?, profileSlug?, label? }. Example: { "comms": { "workspaceId": "<uuid>" } }. Merged per-domain. |
| `reasoning`      | string | no       | Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line.                                                                                                          |

## synap_list_workspaces

**List spaces** · Group: `spaces` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

List the workspaces (domain lenses) you can see, pod-wide — call this to find a workspace id instead of guessing from orient. Each row: id, name, description, workspaceType, your role, accessKind (member | pod_visible), archived, entityCount, and usedByProjectIds (projects that run through it — an INDEX, not an ACL). Link a project to one with synap_project_use_workspace. To learn what a space is FOR and what it knows — its purpose, the kinds it holds, its rules and its skills — PIN it: pass its workspaceId to `synap_orient`, or `synap_set_workspace_focus`; both return that space's `brief`.

| Parameter         | Type    | Required | Description                                      |
| ----------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `includeArchived` | boolean | no       | Include soft-archived workspaces (default false) |
| `appId`           | string  | no       | Optional filter by settings.appId                |

## synap_create_project

**Create project** · Group: `spaces` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Create a project — a cross-cutting lens for an initiative/venture that organizes entities across workspaces (a workspace is a domain lens; a project cuts across them). workspaceId = its HOME workspace (optional). A PROJECT IS A COMMITMENT WITH GRAVITY: never create one per git-repo, per-feature, or per-task — those are entities (task/plan/note). You MUST pass evidenceEntityIds: at least 5 existing entity ids that would belong to this project, or the create is rejected. A project with the same name is reused; a similar one, or the same one still waiting for review, does not block: the create is filed for review showing it, so reuse it instead of making a near-duplicate. An agent call lands as a proposal unless governance has widened it: status="proposed" is SUCCESS — say it is awaiting review, do not retry.

| Parameter           | Type          | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------- | ------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `name`              | string        | yes      | Project display name                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `description`       | string        | no       |                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `workspaceId`       | string        | no       | The project's HOME workspace (optional — falls back to the user's first workspace if omitted).                                                                                                   |
