## synap_list_tracks

**List tracks** · Group: `tracks` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

List a project's TRACKS — the lasting goals it is pursuing (e.g. 'Grow the newsletter', 'Win the first ten clients' inside one project). Work in a track = synap_start_session with its trackId. A track holds a direction, instructions and a goal, and turns workers on; it has no stages and never completes. LEGACY: an old track also follows a project-scoped playbook (its method, with stages), pinned at the version it started with; a new track has none (playbookId null, no stages). Each row: id, name, playbookId, methodVersion, status (active|paused|completed|archived), pausedBy (check|human|null — why a paused track is held), currentStage and stages [{ key, name, position: done|active|not_started, addedAt? }] (addedAt marks a stage added after the start), direction (where it is heading, or null) and kpi ({ label, unit?, target, current?, updatedAt? } or null — current is STATED, updatedAt says when). Archived tracks are omitted unless includeArchived. Find the project id with synap_list_projects.

| Parameter         | Type    | Required | Description                               |
| ----------------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `projectId`       | string  | yes      | Project UUID                              |
| `includeArchived` | boolean | no       | Also list archived tracks. Default false. |

## synap_start_track

**Start track** · Group: `tracks` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Start a TRACK on a project — a LASTING goal (e.g. 'Grow the newsletter'): pass a `name`, a one-line `direction` in the person's words and, only if the person names a number, a `kpi`. List the project's tracks first (synap_list_tracks) and resume a running one rather than starting a twin. Work in it = synap_start_session with its trackId, one session per sitting, for as long as the goal lasts; it is paused or archived, never completed for hitting a number. No method needed and never stages: playbookId (a project-scoped playbook with stages) is OPTIONAL and legacy — omit it. Repeatable work under it = sessions that follow a playbook, or workers a status starts. While the track is active, its agent may work in the spaces the project links. Idempotent per track NAME: a live track of that name comes back with status='exists'; a live track of another method holding the name is refused. Governed: status='proposed' is SUCCESS — say it awaits review, pass on reviewUrl, do not retry. Otherwise status='started' with the track.

| Parameter    | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------ | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `projectId`  | string | yes      | Project UUID                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `playbookId` | string | no       | OPTIONAL, legacy: UUID of a project-scoped playbook (a method with stages). Omit it — a track needs no method.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `name`       | string | no       | The track's name, in the person's words — REQUIRED without a playbookId (with one it defaults to the method's name). Its identity on the project.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `params`     | object | no       | Only with a playbookId: answers to the method's declared params, by param name. A mistyped value or an unknown name is refused; params with no method are refused.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `direction`  | string | no       | Optional: where the track is heading, ONE line in the person's words. May be non-verifiable — the verifiable part is each session's outcomes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `kpi`        | object | no       | Optional number the track steers by: { label, unit?, target, current? } (numbers). Only if the person names one; never invent a metric.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `reasoning`  | string | no       | Why you are starting it, in the person's words — shown to the reviewer. One line.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `sessionId`  | string | no       | OPTIONAL focus-session override. Leave it out and the write is attributed automatically — you do NOT normally pass this. Send it ONLY to disambiguate: when two or more of your focus sessions are open, automatic attribution deliberately declines rather than guess, and this is the only way to say which session the write belongs to. Also the way to JOIN a session another conversation started — automatic attribution never shares one across conversations. A session that isn't yours is ignored, not an error. |

## synap_start_stage_session

**Start stage session** · Group: `tracks` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

LEGACY — for a track with stages; to work in a track, prefer synap_start_session with trackId (on a track with no stages this tool does exactly that). Start the work session for ONE stage of a track — the session a stage OFFERS when the track enters it (synap_advance_track returns it as `offer`). Advancing a track never starts work; call this only when the person wants that step worked on now. Defaults to the track's CURRENT stage; the stage's goal is the session's brief, its expected outputs and criteria are copied on, and the track's params are passed, so a required param nobody answered becomes a question owed to the person. Idempotent: an open session already filed at that stage comes back with status='existing'. Governed: status='proposed' is SUCCESS — say it awaits review, pass on reviewUrl, do not retry.

| Parameter  | Type   | Required | Description                                                               |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trackId`  | string | yes      | Track UUID                                                                |
| `stageKey` | string | no       | The stage KEY to work on. Omit for the track's current stage.             |
| `title`    | string | no       | Optional one-line session name; defaults to the stage's name.             |
| `goal`     | string | no       | Optional outcome in the person's words; defaults to the stage's own goal. |

## synap_advance_track

**Advance track** · Group: `tracks` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

LEGACY — only a track started with a method has stages; a track with none is never advanced (work in it = synap_start_session with trackId). Only with the user. Move a track to one of its method's stages — forward OR back (stages are re-enterable; any stage key synap_list_tracks shows). Refused for a stage the method does not declare, or a completed/archived track. A stage may carry a GATE: a human gate pauses the track and files an approval (`proposalId` on the reply); a check gate measures the sessions filed at the stage being left (at least one closed, every closed one passing its criteria) and otherwise holds the track paused (pausedBy='check', `check.reason` says why) until resumed with synap_set_track_status status='active'. Entering a stage does NOT start work: the reply's `offer` is the session that stage suggests — offer it to the person, and start it with synap_start_stage_session only if they want it. Governed: status='proposed' is SUCCESS — pass on reviewUrl, do not retry.

| Parameter   | Type   | Required | Description                                                         |
| ----------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trackId`   | string | yes      | Track UUID                                                          |
| `toStage`   | string | yes      | The stage KEY to move to (not its display name).                    |
| `reasoning` | string | no       | Why the work moves to this stage — shown to the reviewer. One line. |

## synap_set_track_status

**Set track status** · Group: `tracks` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Pause, resume or archive a track. A track is LASTING: pause it while nobody should work on it (its agent loses access to the project's spaces until it resumes); archive it when the goal is dropped — archived is FINAL (start a new track with synap_start_track). Resuming (status='active') also releases a track a check gate held (pausedBy='check'). A move the table does not allow is refused with the reason. Governed: status='proposed' is SUCCESS — pass on reviewUrl, do not retry.

| Parameter   | Type   | Required | Description                                                              |
| ----------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `trackId`   | string | yes      | Track UUID                                                               |
| `status`    | enum   | yes      | The status to move the track to. One of: `active`, `paused`, `archived`. |
| `reasoning` | string | no       | Why the track changes status — shown to the reviewer. One line.          |

## synap_set_track_params

**Set track params** · Group: `tracks` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

LEGACY (tracks started with a method) — answer (some of) a track's method params — the questions the method DECLARED when the track started (synap_list_tracks returns them as `declaredParams`, with each one's `type`, `required` and any `options`). MERGED onto the answers already given: only the keys you pass change, and a null value clears that answer. A key the method does not declare, or a value of the wrong type, is refused with the reason. Stage sessions started afterwards carry the answers; a required param still unanswered is a question owed to the person. Governed: status='proposed' is SUCCESS — pass on reviewUrl, do not retry.

| Parameter   | Type   | Required | Description                                                        |
| ----------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `trackId`   | string | yes      | Track UUID                                                         |
| `params`    | object | yes      | Answers keyed by the declared param `name`. null clears an answer. |
| `reasoning` | string | no       | Why these answers — shown to the reviewer. One line.               |

## synap_update_track

**Update track** · Group: `tracks` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Set a track's DIRECTION (where it is heading, one line) and/or its KPI (the number it steers by). kpi is MERGED onto the stored one: pass { current } to state the latest value (stamped with when and by whom — it is STATED, never measured), { target } to move the goal, a whole { label, unit?, target, current? } to define one, or null to clear it. direction null clears it. A KPI needs a label and a target. Reaching the target NUDGES the person to re-aim it (a new target) — the track keeps going; never move the target yourself. Governed: status='proposed' is SUCCESS — pass on reviewUrl, do not retry.

| ----------- | -------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trackId`   | string         | yes      | Track UUID                                                                    |
| `direction` | string \| null | no       | One line, in the person's words. null clears it.                              |
| `kpi`       | object \| null | no       | A KPI patch { label?, unit?, target?, current? } (numbers), or null to clear. |
| `reasoning` | string         | no       | Why — shown to the reviewer. One line.                                        |

LEGACY — a track has no stages; only an old track started from a method does. Add a stage to such a RUNNING track — work the method did not foresee. A stage carries a name and an optional goal; what it must yield is declared as `outcomes` on the session worked there, and that is what a check gate measures. A key already declared is refused. | `viewId`           | string        | yes      | View UUID to update                                                                                 |
| `store`            | object        | yes      | Canonical tldraw payload                                                                            |
| `elements`         | array         | no       | Optional elements array                                                                             |
| `embeddedEntities` | array<string> | no       | Optional UUID array of embedded entities                                                            |
| `version`          | number        | yes      | For optimistic locking                                                                              |
| `reasoning`        | string        | no       | Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line. |

## synap_list_views

**List views** · Group: `build` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

List views you own, optionally narrowed by workspaceId, type, or profileId. Call this BEFORE synap_create_view so you do not duplicate an existing board. Owner-only (same floor as hub listViews). Omit filters for the full catalog.

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `detail`      | enum   | no       | lean (default) = a digest to pick an id from (the heavy config/graph omitted, see `note`); full = complete rows — pair with a small limit. One of: `lean`, `full`. |
| `workspaceId` | string | no       | Optional workspace UUID to narrow to. Omit for every view you own.                                                                                                 |
| `type`        | string | no       | Optional view type filter (table, kanban, list, gallery, calendar, bento, masonry, flow).                                                                          |
| `profileId`   | string | no       | Optional profile UUID to filter views scoped to that entity type.                                                                                                  |

## synap_list_widgets

**List compose widgets** · Group: `build` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Live list of what you may place: in a bento (surface "bento", default) or embedded in a document (surface "document"). Call this BEFORE arranging a dashboard or embedding a cell in a document — never guess a key. Each entry has key, requiredConfig, propsSchema (JSON Schema), binding, exampleDirective (the document embed form) and fallback; it covers the built-ins (stat-card, entity-list, view, chart-*, …) plus the cell:<pkg>:<key> / generated:<slug> cells installed on the pod. view needs a saved view UUID (viewId); a profileSlug is not enough. Counts use stat-card. With surface "document" it also returns fences: content languages written as a fenced block (`mermaid diagrams, `math equations, code), each with its aiHint.

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `surface`     | enum   | no       | Where you will place it: bento (dashboard block, default) or document (an embed inside a document). One of: `bento`, `document`. |
| `workspaceId` | string | no       | Optional workspace UUID. Include it so workspace-scoped generated cells appear.                                                  |
