**Get or create channel** · Group: `read` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Get or create a channel. Use mode 'personal' to get the user's personal AI thread for a workspace. Use mode 'by-context' to get/create a thread scoped to an entity or document.

| Parameter           | Type   | Required | Description                                                  |
| ------------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `mode`              | enum   | yes      | One of: `personal`, `by-context`.                            |
| `workspaceId`       | string | yes      |                                                              |
| `contextObjectType` | enum   | no       | Required for mode 'by-context' One of: `entity`, `document`. |
| `contextObjectId`   | string | no       | Required for mode 'by-context'                               |

## synap_post_message

**Post message** · Group: `entry` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Post a message to a Synap channel or thread with optional AI triggering. Handles thread creation from a channelId and can trigger an AI response. triggerAI only starts an agent turn when role is 'user' — pass role:'user' with triggerAI:true to start one. In a session's room (`session.channelId`) this is how you talk to the person: kind 'question' notifies them on their phone; 'update' (default) shows in-app only; an @mention of them notifies too. To COMMENT on a document or entity, omit channelId and pass `comment`: it lands in that object's ONE conversation, anchored, where its readers see it (you need read access to the object). Comments are speech: to change the document, propose an edit instead.

| Parameter        | Type                                           | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idempotencyKey` | string                                         | no       | Optional: a stable key so a retry returns the PRIOR message, not a duplicate. Plain posts also dedup on identical content automatically — EXCEPT a post that triggers the AI (triggerAI:true), which never content-dedups (two identical prompts are two real turns); pass a key there for at-most-once turn semantics.                                                                |
| `channelId`      | string                                         | no       | Channel UUID to post into                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `content`        | string                                         | yes      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `role`           | enum                                           | no       | One of: `user`, `assistant`, `system`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `triggerAI`      | boolean                                        | no       | Set true to trigger an AI response after posting                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `kind`           | enum                                           | no       | 'question' when you need the person's answer (pair it with `slotLabel` + an `ask` so they get yes/no or options, not a bare button) — in a session room it pushes a notification to them (once per session per few hours). 'update' for progress and results — in-app only, never a push. One of: `question`, `update`.                                                                |
| `slotLabel`      | string                                         | no       | With kind 'question': the label of the session output the question is about. The question is filed ON that output (it becomes the person's, with your question as its why), so it shows as a card they can answer; their answer is recorded as its `answer` and hands it back to you.                                                                                                  |
| `ask`            | object \| object \| object \| object \| object | no       | With kind 'question' + slotLabel: HOW the person answers — 'confirm' (yes/no), 'choose' (1-8 options, ≤1 recommended), 'form' (small flat form; never a secret), 'act' (a physical/world task only; they answer 'I did this'), 'provide' (connection {service} \| file {accept} \| secret {name}, via the vault). Prefer confirm/choose for any decision. Omit for a free-text answer. |
| `comment`        | object                                         | no       | Instead of channelId: a comment on an object. EITHER `anchor` (open a thread) OR `replyTo` (reply in one).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

## synap_revise_proposal

**Revise proposal** · Group: `governance` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Amend a pending proposal you authored (e.g. after user feedback): its summary, its reasoning, and/or the payload it will actually apply. A pending playbook proposal (create or update) is amended with patch {kind:'inner', fields:{ stages, goalTemplate, params, … }}; the revised payload is checked like the playbook write itself, so a bad one is refused now, not at approval. Does not re-run the event pipeline, and does NOT approve it — a human still decides.

| Parameter    | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------ | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `proposalId` | string | yes      | Proposal UUID, as returned verbatim by synap_list_proposals. A leading fragment of one also resolves, but pass the full id you were given — do not shorten it yourself.                                                                   |
| `summary`    | string | no       | The human-readable summary a reviewer reads when deciding.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `reasoning`  | string | no       | Why this change is being requested.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `patch`      | object | no       | Amend WHAT WILL BE APPLIED, not just the narrative. Use this whenever you change the summary to describe different content — a summary that no longer matches the payload is worse than no revision, because the human reads the summary. |

## synap_reject_proposal

**Reject proposal** · Group: `governance` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Reject a pending proposal so the queued change never lands — withdraw a write you now know is wrong (a duplicate, a superseded plan, a mistaken read) instead of leaving it in the user's review queue. Give a `reason`: it is recorded on the proposal and feeds your agent scorecard. There is deliberately NO approve tool: approval is the HUMAN step (an agent key that approved its own write would be self-approving) — point the user at the proposal's review link instead. Rejecting is safe by the same logic in reverse: it only PREVENTS a pending change from landing, so it carries no self-approval or undo risk. Only a still-pending proposal can be rejected.

| Parameter    | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------ | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `proposalId` | string | yes      | Proposal UUID, as returned verbatim by synap_list_proposals. A leading fragment of one also resolves, but pass the full id you were given — do not shorten it yourself.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `reason`     | string | no       | Why you are rejecting it (recorded on the proposal). Always give one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `reasonCode` | enum   | no       | Optional structured cause, one of the fixed set — recorded alongside `reason` and fed to the calibration/scorecard loop. Use `other` (or omit) when none fits and rely on the free-text `reason`. One of: `wrong_entity`, `duplicate`, `wrong_kind_or_facet`, `wrong_link_type`, `wrong_workspace`, `bad_data`, `not_relevant`, `other`. |

## synap_request_deploy_approval

**Request deploy approval** · Group: `governance` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Ask the person to approve shipping ONE verified commit — the dev loop's deploy gate. Files a `dev.deploy_approval` proposal on your session: it is ALWAYS a proposal (`status: 'proposed'` is the success outcome), and only the person can approve it — there is no approve tool. Call it after the gate passed on the exact commit you will ship, with that commit's full sha, the gate's headline (`gateReport`), where it goes (`targetHost`) and the command you will run (`deployCommand`, shown to the reviewer; the pod never runs it). On approval the session records the decision (who, when, which commit) and moves past its deploy stage; then you deploy that commit and nothing else. Rejected, or a new commit since: fix, re-run the gate and ask again. Refused (`error`) when the session is not yours or the payload is malformed — read the message and resend.

| Parameter       | Type   | Required | Description                                                                              |
| --------------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sessionId`     | string | yes      | Your focus session (UUID) — the one the work happened in.                                |
| `repo`          | string | yes      | Repository the commit is in (path or slug).                                              |
| `branch`        | string | yes      | Branch of the commit.                                                                    |
| `commitSha`     | string | yes      | The exact commit to ship — hex git object id (7–64 chars; send the full sha).            |
| `gateReport`    | object | yes      | Headline of the verification that passed on THIS commit — the evidence the ask rests on. |
| `targetHost`    | string | yes      | Human label of the deploy target, e.g. 'pod-prod (eve)'.                                 |
| `deployCommand` | string | yes      | The command you will run once approved. Disclosure only — the pod never executes it.     |

## synap_find

**Find what can do this** · Group: `read` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

What can do this, and where does it belong? Searches the pod's runnable verbs, the abstract-intent axis, the user's playbooks and their spaces (with the kinds to write there) in ONE call, and returns each match WITH its argument schema, so you can run it without a second lookup. Pass `intent` as free text (not the closed intent vocabulary). A block that is absent was not searched; `matches: []` means it was searched and nothing fit. Matching is lexical, so a miss is never proof of absence — `coverage` says how much was searched and `noConfidentMatch` carries the escalation ladder. Run a hit with synap_run_capability (verbId) or synap_run_playbook (playbook id).

| Parameter     | Type        | Required | Description                                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | ----------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `intent`      | string      | yes      | What you want to DO, in your own words (e.g. 'clean up duplicate contacts'). Keep the NOUN — it is the most discriminating word. |
| `workspaceId` | string      | no       | Optional workspace lens. Omit for pod altitude, which is what 'what can this pod do?' usually means.                             |
| `catalogs`    | array<enum> | no       | Which catalogs to search. Omit for all. A catalog you leave out is ABSENT from the result, not empty.                            |
| `limit`       | number      | no       | Max matches per catalog (default 5).                                                                                             |

## synap_list_capabilities

**List tools** · Group: `capabilities` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Discover what the user can actually DO. Returns a SECTIONED view: `integrations` (their connected services + tools, one per name, each with its `verbs` nested — e.g. google → gmail_send, gmail_search, calendar_list; the verb `id` is what you pass to synap_run_capability), `skills` (standalone runnable skills), and `commands`. Each integration shows `connection.connected` (needs connecting if false) and each verb shows `granted`/`effectiveExecMode` (a not-yet-granted verb must be enabled in Settings → Capabilities). Core built-in tools (already available to you directly as MCP tools) and teaching docs are folded out of this actionable view BY DEFAULT and only COUNTED under `excluded` — pass kind:"builtin-tool" or kind:"teaching-doc" to list them here instead, or synap_load_skill("catalog") for every teaching doc grouped by topic. Pass `query` to search across integrations/verbs/skills (e.g. query:"send email").

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `workspaceId` | string | no       | Workspace UUID                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `query`       | string | no       | Search text (e.g. 'send email', 'calendar'). Ranks + narrows the result instead of returning the full unfiltered dump.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `kind`        | string | no       | Optional exact kind filter: tool \| skill \| command \| source-provider \| builtin-tool \| teaching-doc.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `containerId` | string | no       | Only rows belonging to this capability pack (the `containerId` on integrations/skills, or `builtInPack.containerId`). The default view summarises Synap Core's first-party verbs as ONE `builtInPack` line — pass its containerId to list them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `intent`      | string | no       | Reverse lookup by INTENT slug — what you want to DO, without knowing the vendor. A registry slug (the seed includes search_external, send_message, capture_into_pod, and the rest of the original 13). Returns the concrete verb ids that serve it (pass one to synap_run_capability). Takes precedence over `query`/`kind`/`limit`. An unknown slug is an error from the registry, not an empty list. An empty match list means the slug is known and nothing installed declares it yet — scan without `intent` before concluding the pod cannot do this. |
| `limit`       | number | no       | Max entries to return (default 20 when `query` is set; unset otherwise).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

## synap_run_capability

**Run tool** · Group: `capabilities` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: true · openWorldHint: true

Run a registered capability verb (discover via synap_list_capabilities) with dynamic inputs — e.g. send an email, search Gmail, create a calendar event. Pass verbId + parameters. A DRAFT (un-enabled) capability is refused — ask the user to enable it first. Governed like any write: an ungranted verb comes back as `{ kind: "proposed", proposalId, reviewUrl }` instead of running — that is SUCCESS, not an error. You MUST surface the `reviewUrl` as a clickable link in your reply (never just say 'proposed' with no link) — e.g. "Queued that email send for your review: [Review proposal](reviewUrl)" — and continue the conversation without waiting for approval.

| Parameter            | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `verbId`             | string | no       | The capability name from synap_list_capabilities (e.g. 'gmail_send'). Alternatively pass skillId.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `skillId`            | string | no       | Direct backing-skill UUID (alternative to verbId).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `parameters`         | object | no       | The capability's inputs — e.g. { to, subject, body } for gmail_send, { query } for gmail_search.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `workspaceId`        | string | yes      | Workspace UUID                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `connectionSelector` | object | no       | Which of the capability's connections this run uses, when it has more than one. `connectionId` names a specific connection; `contextObjectId` names the connection bound to that context object. Omit to use the only/default connection — a selector matching nothing fails the run. |
| `idempotencyKey`     | string | no       | Optional: a stable key that correlates retries of THIS run. Note: a direct capability run has NO automatic content dedup — a retried call CAN produce a second external effect (e.g. a second send). Pass a key when the effect must be at-most-once; the key is recorded on the run. |

## synap_create_verb

**Create verb** · Group: `capabilities` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Add a new DECLARATIVE verb (a deterministic provider HTTP call — no code execution) to an ALREADY-INSTALLED, already-credentialed tool — e.g. teach 'apify_api' a new 'apify_search_reddit_actors' verb without a dev-session/redeploy. Creates a kind='declarative' skill only; rejects any request implying code/instruction/builtin execution. `toolName` MUST already exist (installed + visible to the caller) or this is refused — it never creates a new tool/connection as a side effect. Governed the same as every other write: may return status='proposed' for review. Discover installed tools with synap_list_capabilities first.

| Parameter       | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `toolName`      | string | yes      | The NAME of the already-installed tool this verb calls (e.g. 'apify_api'). Must already exist — this tool never creates a new tool/connection. |
| `verbName`      | string | yes      | Stable name for the new verb/skill (e.g. 'apify_search_reddit_actors').                                                                        |
| `description`   | string | no       | What the verb does and when to use it.                                                                                                         |
| `method`        | enum   | yes      | HTTP method the provider call uses. One of: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`.                                                           |
| `pathTemplate`  | string | yes      | Request path with {{param}} interpolation, e.g. '/v2/acts/{{actorId}}/runs'.                                                                   |
| `query`         | object | no       | Query params; values may be '{{param}}'; arrays become repeated query keys.                                                                    |
| `body`          | object | no       | Request body template; values may be '{{param}}'.                                                                                              |
| `responseShape` | object | no       | How to shape the provider's raw response (collectionPath, item, scalar, headers dot-paths).                                                    |
| `parameters`    | object | no       | The verb's own runtime parameter schema using the shorthand type system, e.g. { query: "string", limit: "number?" }.                           |
| `workspaceId`   | string | no       | Optional workspace UUID to scope the new verb to (default: pod-wide).                                                                          |

## synap_list_automations

**List rules** · Group: `capabilities` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

List automations (WHEN-triggered flows) visible in a workspace — the reactive rules a user has set up (e.g. 'on new lead → draft a follow-up', 'every morning → recap yesterday'). Each entry has its id (pass to synap_trigger_automation), name, triggerType (event | cron | webhook | manual), and status (active | draft | paused | error). Read-only. Call this to discover what already reacts BEFORE creating a new automation. Omit workspaceId to list everything accessible.

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `detail`      | enum   | no       | lean (default) = a digest to pick an id from (the heavy config/graph omitted, see `note`); full = complete rows — pair with a small limit. One of: `lean`, `full`. |
| `workspaceId` | string | no       | Optional workspace UUID to narrow to (pod-wide automations are always included). Omit for all accessible.                                                          |
| `status`      | enum   | no       | Optional status filter. One of: `draft`, `active`, `paused`, `error`.                                                                                              |
| `limit`       | number | no       | Max entries to return (default 50).                                                                                                                                |

## synap_trigger_automation

**Run rule now** · Group: `capabilities` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: true · openWorldHint: true

Run an existing automation NOW, on demand (discover ids via synap_list_automations) — e.g. fire a 'daily client recap' immediately instead of waiting for its schedule. Pass the automation id; optionally a payload injected as the run's trigger.payload. This is a RUN, not a proposal: it returns { status: 'triggered', runId } once enqueued (gated by your write access to the automation's workspace). Any entity writes the run then performs are separately reviewed under the automation's own governance. A draft automation is runnable on demand this way; paused/error non-manual ones are refused.

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                    |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `id`          | string | yes      | UUID of the automation to trigger.                                                                                             |
| `payload`     | object | no       | Optional data injected as trigger.payload in the run context (e.g. { entityId } to bind the run to a subject).                 |
| `workspaceId` | string | no       | Optional workspace lens. When set, only automations in that workspace can be triggered; omit to trigger a pod-wide automation. |
| `reasoning`   | string | no       | Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line.                            |

## synap_create_automation

**Create rule flow (advanced)** · Group: `capabilities` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Create an automation — a WHEN→THEN flow that reacts to a trigger (event | cron | webhook | manual) by running a flow of steps. Use for repeatable reactions ('every morning recap each client', 'on new deal notify the channel'). Governed the same as every write: an agent create returns status='proposed' for review; on approval it becomes ACTIVE (live) — not a stuck draft. Provide the trigger, a flowDefinition ({ nodes, edges }), and a dataContract — the contract is REQUIRED for agent-authored automations (which this always is) and the create door rejects the automation without a valid one. For a cron trigger put the schedule in triggerConfig.expression (5-field cron). Discover what already exists with synap_list_automations first. Creates it on this pod only; an official template is written in the catalog and published with `synap catalog publish --official`.

| Parameter        | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`           | string | yes      | Automation display name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `description`    | string | no       | What this automation does.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `triggerType`    | enum   | yes      | WHEN it fires: 'event' (something happened, e.g. entity created), 'cron' (schedule — put the 5-field expression in triggerConfig.expression), 'webhook' (external call), 'manual' (only via synap_trigger_automation). One of: `event`, `cron`, `webhook`, `manual`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `triggerConfig`  | object | no       | Trigger settings. cron → { expression: '0 9 * * *' }. event → { eventPattern: 'entity.create.completed', filters: { ... } }. FILTERS GRAMMAR (enforced — a filter the runtime cannot evaluate is REJECTED, because an automation with an unevaluable filter installs as 'active' and then never fires): each key is a dot-notation path into the event data ('profileSlug', 'channel.contextObjectType'); each value is EITHER a plain string/number/boolean/null (exact match) OR an operator object — $eq, $ne, $in (non-empty array), $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte (numeric). E.g. { profileSlug: 'person' }, { profileSlug: { $in: ['person','contact'] } }, { score: { $gt: 30 } }. ENTITY PROPERTIES ARE FLAT: 'entity.update.completed' spreads the entity's changed properties onto event data under their BARE slug, so the key is 'score' — NOT 'properties.score', which resolves to undefined and silently never matches. A bare array value and a nested object value are BOTH rejected: use $in for several values, and a dot-notation key to reach nested data. |
| `flowDefinition` | object | yes      | The THEN flow: { nodes: [...], edges: [...] }. Nodes are the steps; edges wire them in order. A step of type 'capability' MUST name a verb that actually exists — data.verbId is the backing skill's NAME (e.g. 'ai.generate'), not a UUID, and the create is REJECTED if it does not resolve for you (data.capabilityId is optional; omit it and the verb alone resolves). Check with synap_list_capabilities before authoring capability steps.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `status`         | enum   | no       | Defaults to 'active' (live once approved). One of: `draft`, `active`, `paused`, `error`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `resultRouting`  | enum   | no       | Optional: where run results are posted. 'per_entity' = the subject entity's own channel, 'per_type' = one channel per entity type, 'trigger' = the triggering channel. One of: `per_type`, `per_entity`, `trigger`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `metadata`       | object | yes      | Metadata bag. REQUIRED here: `dataContract` — this tool is always agent-authored, and automations.create REJECTS an agent-authored automation whose metadata carries no valid contract. Any other keys you add are kept as-is.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `workspaceId`    | string | no       | Optional workspace to scope to (default pod-wide).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## synap_create_rule

**Create rule** · Group: `governance` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Turn a stated standing intent into a RULE — the COMPILED door, and the one to reach for whenever the user says 'always…', 'from now on…', 'never…', 'every Monday…', or states a preference that should outlive this conversation. Send their own words as `intent`.
• `intent` alone → a FACT rule: durable prose ('Acme prefers async') that any agent reads later while reasoning. Legitimate and complete.
• `intent` + `sentence` → BEHAVIOUR: the door compiles your WHEN/WHERE/THEN into a real automation, or refuses. A rule that describes something running is never stored as prose that cannot run.
USE THIS INSTEAD OF synap_create_automation / synap_create_skill for a standing intent. Those are raw primitives — they persist whatever you hand them, so a bad trigger installs 'active' and silently never fires, and an instruction skill only ever sits there as text. This door verifies the compiled artifact against the runtime BEFORE anything is saved. (Reach for synap_create_automation directly only when you are authoring a flow that is not a user-stated rule — a multi-step pipeline with its own data contract.)
WHAT IT REJECTS, and why each rejection is real: a WHEN naming an event no emitter produces (the automation could never match); a WHERE row with a field but no value (dropping it would widen the rule beyond what was written); a THEN with no configured action (a trigger wired to nothing); `run_command` (the command step has no receiver and throws every run — use an AI step). A refusal comes back as status='denied' with `failure.clause` (WHEN | WHERE | THEN) and a reason written for a human. FIX THAT CLAUSE AND RESEND — it is a verdict, not a transient error, and re-sending it unchanged will fail identically.
If the intent describes something that should run and you send no `sentence`, the receipt carries `needsBehaviour` — the rule was saved as prose and will not execute; say so rather than reporting it as in effect.
Scope: pod-wide by default; pass `workspaceId` for a domain rule, `projectId` for the cross-cutting lens. A `projectId` limit is only enforceable on WHEN events that carry a project — entity._, entity_facet._, external_message._, channel_message._, focus_session._, proposal._ — and is REFUSED (status='denied', clause WHEN) on any other trigger (e.g. a schedule); drop the project or pick one of those events. `expiresAt` makes the rule stop applying — pass one whenever the intent is situational ('while we're in the launch push'), because a standing rule with no expiry is one the user must remember to revoke.
Governed like every write: status='proposed' is SUCCESS, not an error — surface the returned link as a markdown link and never report a proposed rule as already in effect.

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `intent`      | string | yes      | The rule in the user's own words — this IS the rule an agent reads later, so keep their phrasing rather than paraphrasing it into a spec.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `sentence`    | object | no       | The rule's structured WHEN / WHERE / THEN. Send it when the rule should DO something — the door compiles it into a live automation or REFUSES naming the clause that failed. Omit it for a prose-only FACT rule. All three keys are required when you send it (`conditions` and `actions` may be empty arrays, but an empty `actions` is refused as 'no THEN'). |
| `scope`       | enum   | no       | Where the rule applies. Defaults to 'workspace' when a workspaceId resolves, otherwise 'pod' (everywhere). One of: `pod`, `workspace`, `user`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `workspaceId` | string | no       | Optional workspace lens. Omit for a pod-wide rule; the ambient workspace focus is used when set.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `projectId`   | string | no       | Optional cross-cutting project lens — composes with the workspace lens.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `expiresAt`   | string | no       | ISO-8601 instant with offset (e.g. '2026-12-31T00:00:00Z') after which the rule stops applying. A non-instant is refused rather than stored.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

## synap_update_rule

**Update rule** · Group: `governance` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Propose a CORRECTION to an existing rule — the governed edit door, the same one the app's rule editor uses. Reach for it when a rule you (or anyone) wrote no longer matches the facts: change its wording, its WHEN/WHERE/THEN, its scope or its review date. Never delete-and-recreate a rule to change it — that loses its id, its run history and its lineage.
FULL SHAPE, not a patch: send the rule as it should be stored. `intent` and `scope` are REQUIRED and replace the stored ones (send the old wording/scope unchanged if you are only fixing the sentence). `expiresAt` and `sentence` have THREE states: omit to KEEP the stored value, `null` to CLEAR it (a `null` sentence makes the rule prose-only and retires its automation), a value to REPLACE it. `draft` defaults to false — editing a draft rule therefore ACTIVATES it, which recompiles the sentence and is refused by clause if it still has a hole; pass `draft: true` to keep it a draft.
`ruleId`: the `ruleId` on synap_create_rule's receipt. If that create came back `proposed`, call synap_get_proposal with its proposalId after a person approved it — the id is `data.materialized.ruleId`. There is no dedicated rule listing on MCP. A workspace rule is only found under its workspace (pass its `workspaceId`); `not_found` means no rule with that id is visible to you.
Refusals are the same as synap_create_rule's: status='denied' with `failure.clause` (WHEN | WHERE | THEN) — fix that clause and resend.
Governed like every write: status='proposed' is SUCCESS, not an error — nothing changes until a person approves it. Surface the returned link as a markdown link and never report a proposed edit as already in effect.

| Parameter     | Type           | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | -------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ruleId`      | string         | yes      | UUID of the rule to edit (the `ruleId` from synap_create_rule's receipt, or `data.materialized.ruleId` on its approved proposal).                                                                                                |
| `intent`      | string         | yes      | The rule's wording as it should READ after the edit — in the user's own words. Required: it replaces the stored intent.                                                                                                          |
| `sentence`    | object \| null | no       | The WHEN / WHERE / THEN as it should be after the edit — same grammar as synap_create_rule's `sentence`. OMIT to keep the stored one (it is recompiled); `null` REMOVES the behaviour (prose-only rule, its automation retired). |
| `scope`       | enum           | yes      | Where the rule applies AFTER the edit. Required — send the current scope to keep it. One of: `pod`, `workspace`, `user`.                                                                                                         |
| `workspaceId` | string         | no       | The rule's workspace, for a workspace-scoped rule (the ambient workspace focus is used when omitted). Also the lens the rule is looked up in.                                                                                    |
| `projectId`   | string         | no       | Optional cross-cutting project lens — same limits as on synap_create_rule.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `expiresAt`   | string \| null | no       | ISO-8601 instant with offset after which the rule stops applying. OMIT to keep the stored date; `null` clears it.                                                                                                                |
| `draft`       | boolean        | no       | true keeps (or returns) the rule to DRAFT — nothing compiled, nothing can fire. Omitted/false = live: a draft is ACTIVATED (recompiled, refused by clause if it has a hole).                                                     |

## synap_run_playbook

**Run template** · Group: `build` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: true · openWorldHint: true

LAUNCH a playbook via its executor (discover via synap_list_playbooks) — instantiates a session + run channel + playbook_run and dispatches to the playbook's executor (is-agent | external-agent | hybrid). Pass playbookId OR an unambiguous playbookName/name (multi-match returns candidates — never a silent pick). Write home: workspaceId if set, else the playbook's workspace, else subject/session; pod-wide playbooks with no home reject (pass workspaceId). This LAUNCHES the executor — it is not the same as opening a working session from the template. Governed, with THREE normal outcomes: status="proposed" (an agent launch awaits approval — SUCCESS, pass on reviewUrl, do not retry), status="blocked" (nothing ran: the playbook uses skills that are not enabled yet; `unenabledSkills` names them and `enableProposals` carries ONE enable request per pack — relay the message and run it again only after that is approved), status="draft" (an agent launch the gate allowed: the run is the person's DRAFT and does NOT start until they accept it in their sessions — `session` is returned, `run` is null; tell the person, do not retry), status="running" (it started; `run` + `session` are returned), status="skipped" (nothing ran and nothing is queued — the record's last run failed recently and is cooling down, or no pinned record was ready; read `message`, do not retry in a loop and do not report it as started).

| Parameter      | Type          | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------- | ------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `playbookId`   | string        | no       | UUID of the playbook to run. Provide this OR playbookName/name.                                                                                                                                           |
| `playbookName` | string        | no       | Public name of the playbook (case-insensitive). Must be unique among playbooks you can see; ambiguous names return candidates with id + workspaceId.                                                      |
| `name`         | string        | no       | Alias for playbookName.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `params`       | object        | no       | Values for the playbook's declared params, filled into its goalTemplate's {name} placeholders (e.g. { market: 'EU fintech' }).                                                                            |
| `subjectId`    | string        | no       | Optional entity UUID to bind this run to (the run's subject lens). Also used as write-home fallback for pod-wide playbooks.                                                                               |
| `agentIds`     | array<string> | no       | Optional agent ids to staff the run with.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `reasoning`    | string        | no       | Why you're launching this — surfaced on the review proposal.                                                                                                                                              |
| `workspaceId`  | string        | no       | Write workspace for the run. Optional when the playbook is already workspace-scoped; required for pod-wide playbooks unless subject/session supplies a home. Never falls back to an arbitrary membership. |
| `projectId`    | string        | no       | Optional project UUID to file the run into. Must be a project you can see.                                                                                                                                |
| `trackId`      | string        | no       | Optional track UUID (synap_list_tracks) — the method, inside a project, this run advances. Implies its project; a different projectId is refused.                                                         |

## synap_create_skill

**Create tool (skill)** · Group: `build` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Author a skill: Documentation (always) + OPTIONAL code. Send `body` alone for a TEACHING skill — reusable prose (a process, a checklist, a house style) that any agent later pulls with synap_load_skill; a teaching skill needs a `slug`, because that is the ref load_skill resolves. Send `code` for a runnable sandboxed executable, or both. `kind` is derived from code presence — do not guess it. For a deterministic provider HTTP call on an already-installed tool use synap_create_verb instead. Governed like every write: an agent create returns status='proposed'. An agent-authored skill is born UNAPPROVED either way and does NOT load or run until the owner approves it — code executes, and instruction prose lands in a future agent's system prompt, so both need a deliberate human OK. Creates it on this pod only; an official template is written in the catalog and published with `synap catalog publish --official`.

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`        | string | yes      | Stable skill name (e.g. 'normalize_phone_numbers').                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `description` | string | no       | One line: what it does + when to use it.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `slug`        | string | no       | Stable ref that synap_load_skill resolves, lowercase path segments (e.g. 'biz/business-plan'). REQUIRED for a documentation-only skill — without it the skill is authored but unreachable. Pod-wide unique; 'system/' is reserved for seeded skills. |
| `code`        | string | no       | Optional executable source (runs sandboxed). Present ⇒ the skill is runnable; absent ⇒ it is a teaching skill.                                                                                                                                       |
| `body`        | string | no       | Markdown documentation — for a teaching skill this IS the skill: the process/checklist/style an agent should follow. For a code skill, how it works, inputs/outputs, when to use it. Required unless `code` is given.                                |
| `parameters`  | object | no       | Optional runtime parameter schema (shorthand types, e.g. { input: 'string', count: 'number?' }).                                                                                                                                                     |
| `workspaceId` | string | no       | Optional workspace to scope the skill to (default: pod-wide).                                                                                                                                                                                        |

## synap_update_skill

**Update skill** · Group: `build` · readOnlyHint: false · destructiveHint: false · openWorldHint: false

Revise an existing skill on this pod — its `body` (the teaching prose), `description` or `name` — by `slug` (the ref synap_load_skill resolves) or `id`. Use it when a skill you authored goes stale; never create a second skill under a new slug as a twin. Governed like every write: status='proposed' is success. An agent rewrite of a skill's body is UNAPPROVED until the owner approves it again — that prose lands in future agents' prompts — so do not report it as live.

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                                               |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `slug`        | string | no       | The skill's slug (e.g. 'biz/business-plan').                                              |
| `id`          | string | no       | The skill's UUID — instead of `slug`.                                                     |
| `body`        | string | no       | The full new Markdown body — it REPLACES the old one, so send the whole text, not a diff. |
| `description` | string | no       | One line: what it does + when to use it.                                                  |
| `name`        | string | no       | New display name.                                                                         |

## synap_load_skill

**Load skill** · Group: `entry` · readOnlyHint: true · openWorldHint: false

Load the full body of a seeded teaching skill (the L2 tier behind the one-line summaries you see on other tools' descriptions and in the catalog). Pass a `system/<package>/<stem>` slug, a bare stem (e.g. 'document-embeds'), or 'catalog' to list every available skill grouped by topic. Need a tool you do not see? Pass a tool group — 'tools:read', 'tools:data', 'tools:sessions', 'tools:governance', 'tools:schema', 'tools:spaces', 'tools:tracks', 'tools:build', 'tools:capabilities' — or 'tools:builder' for every tool; a skill that teaches a group unlocks it too.

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ref`         | string | yes      | A skill slug/stem (e.g. 'document-embeds', 'system/synap/document-embeds'), 'catalog', or a tool group ('tools:tracks'; 'tools:builder' = every tool).                          |
| `workspaceId` | string | no       | Optional: also include this workspace's skills (you must be a member). Omit to use your declared workspace focus, if any; otherwise only pod-wide and your own skills are read. |
